jobs.title: Deputy Director of State Policy & Advocacy
jobs.description:
**JOB POSTING: Deputy Director of State Policy \& Advocacy**  

  

The Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA) is a nonprofit organization founded in 1986\. CHIRLA is a California leader with national impact made of diverse immigrant families and individuals who act as agents of social change to achieve a world with freedom of mobility, full human rights, and true participatory democracy. CHIRLA organizes and serves individuals, institutions, and coalitions to build power, transform public opinions, and change policies to achieve full human, civil and labor rights. Guided by power, love, and vision of our community, CHIRLA embraces and drives progressive social change.  

  

**POSITION DESCRIPTION:**  

  

The Deputy Director of State Policy \& Advocacy plays a key role in an exciting team who is charged with planning and executing both long term and short\-term direction of the organization’s policy agenda. The Deputy Director will collaborate and assist in leading future projects to expand and support the work being done across the state. The Deputy Director will lead in the strategic planning to maintain and cultivate relationships with state elected officials, agency directors, and Governor’s office. The Deputy Director oversees the contract lobbyist and policy staff base in the Sacramento office. The ideal candidate will work successfully with CHIRLA’s California\-based staff to engage our membership base in the development and advancement of CHIRLA’s policy advocacy agenda.  

  

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

**EXTERNAL PROGRAM PRIORITIES*** In collaboration with Director of Policy and Advocacy, Executive Director and consultation with membership base create of annual state policy agenda.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy to lead CHIRLA’s state policy agenda.
* Under the supervision of the Director of Policy and Advocacy, manage CHIRLA’s support/oppose/neutral positions to legislative/regulatory/budget proposals.
* Advance and implement CHIRLA goals and objectives as they are determined by the organization.
* Assist in developing legislative/regulatory/budget proposals to advance CHIRLA’s agenda.
* Cultivate and maintain positive working relationships with Members of State Legislature, Constitutional Offices, Agencies and Governor’s office.
* Responsible for securing regular meet\-and\-greets and providing policy analysis to lawmakers and their staff.
* Represent CHIRLA’s position at committee hearings, press conferences, and/or legislative meetings.
* Develop and maintain alliances with immigrant networks to advance CHIRLA’s policy agenda.
* As appropriate, work with the immediate supervisor to develop and implement advocacy strategies and events (to include legislative visits, advocacy days, letters, and call\-in campaigns, media relations, hearings, actions, etc.)
* Develop and provide updates, talking points, action alerts, sample letters, etc. as part of advocacy strategies.
* Support CHIRLA staff by providing research and analysis on issues pertaining to immigrant communities.

**INTERNAL PROGRAM PRIORITIES*** Produce state legislative research, developing policy fact sheets, and talking points.
* Monitor, manage and analyze and summarize propose and/or new laws and regulations negatively/positively impacting immigrants.
* Develop monthly content for CHIRLA’s Al Dìa policy newsletter.
* Monitor and analyze state trends and issues related to immigration and ensure a proactive focus on pro\-immigrant policies.
* Monitor, analyze and summarize propose and/or new laws and regulations negatively/positively impacting immigrants.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy, Director of Organizing and coalition partners to facilitate legislative visits and lobby days that engage immigrants directly impacted by our nation’s immigration laws.
* Work with the Director of Policy and Advocacy and Deputy Director for the Southern Region and Bi\-National Policy in the monitoring and advancement of California border and binational priority policy issues
* Research, analyze and write policy reports and briefing documents on diverse immigrant and immigration issues.
* Supervise and evaluate any staff or policy interns’ performance utilizing CHIRLA’s performance measures on an annual basis.
* Provide regular updates on policy work through progress reports and analysis.
* Create a work plan and confer with the Supervisor as necessary.
* Responsible for ensuring that CHIRLA’s Director of Policy and Advocacy and Executive Director are briefed and knowledgeable about CHIRLA’s state agenda and strategy.
* Meet fundraising and membership goals for CHIRLA’s membership drive and annual Gala.
* Contribute to other program projects as needed.

**SKILLS AND QUALIFICATION:**  

**Required:*** Bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* At least five years of legislative experience in the State Capitol.
* At least five years of advocacy or campaign experience.
* Must be Bilingual English/Spanish with excellent oral communication, public speaking.
* Excellent research and policy development skills.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills in both English and Spanish.
* Deep knowledge of how the state of California government and its branch’s function.
* Broad strategic vision that encompasses public policy with an immigration lens.
* Proven experience in a non\-profit organization or policy firm preferred.
* Strong knowledge of and experience with regional, state, and federal policy advocacy immigration related stakeholders.
* Strong commitment and passion to building immigrant power within a broader strategy toward achieving social, economic, and racial justice.
* Position requires an employee to use his or her personal vehicle to travel between worksites including District of Columbia, Sacramento and Los Angeles.
* Excellent management and supervisory skills

**Preferred:**

* Engagement in immigrant rights and related issues is essential.

jobs.title: Co-Executive Director in Administration
jobs.description:
**Aunt Lute Books Co\-Executive Director in Administration Job Posting**

**About the Organization**

Aunt Lute Books is a 44\-year\-old non profit, intersectional feminist press dedicated to publishing literature by writers who have traditionally been underrepresented or excluded from the literary canon. For more than four decades, Aunt Lute has championed bold, boundary\-pushing fiction, to create space for voices and perspectives too often marginalized within mainstream publishing.

**About the Position**

Aunt Lute is seeking a motivated and collaborative **Co\-Executive Director in Administration** to help co\-lead the organization through its next stage of growth and sustainability. This part\-time position (20\-22 hours per week) works in partnership with the Co\-Executive Director in Operations. The Co\-Executive Director in Administration will focus primarily on fundraising, grant writing and resource development, financial oversight, organizational growth and strategic planning, community engagement and Board relations. They will uphold Aunt Lute’s mission and values in their leadership and decision\-making. This is a hybrid position based in San Francisco. Ideally, candidates should be able to work in\-person once a week and attend events.

*\*See Addendum below for Co\-Executive Director in Operations responsibilities.*

**Job Responsibilities:**

Development

* In collaboration with the Board of Directors, creating and implementing fundraising plans that primarily focus on private foundations and individual annual donors.
* Working closely with staff and Board to accomplish revenue goals consisting of major gifts, foundation and government grants.

Financial Management

* Having a daily knowledge of where financial matters stand for the organization, which includes providing transparent fiscal stewardship that maintains a positive financial position and adequate control and accounting of all funds.
* Develop and propose an annual budget to the Board for their approval.
* Working with our accounting consultant to reconcile accounts and to write tax reports including city, state, and federal reports as required.

Organizational Growth

* With the Board of Directors, creating short\- and long\-term strategic plans in support of Aunt Lute’s mission and documenting progress towards achieving them.
* Developing and improving organizational infrastructure, including business processes, systems, policies, and tools, to maximize efficiency and future growth.

Community Engagement/Outreach

* Participating in relevant community events and cultivating speaking skills to deepen local networks, engage new donors, and expand community presence.
* Developing and nurturing positive relationships with other arts and cultural organizations.
* Supporting staff in planning and executing events sponsored by Aunt Lute in partnership with mission\-aligned organizations.
* Practice feminist leadership styles and ability to engage with racial/gender equity organizations.

Staff Management

* Work with the Co\-ED in Operations to manage the recruitment, employment, and release of all personnel while implementing sound human resource practices.
* Co\-managing the oversight of employee performance and delegating responsibilities.
* Promoting a work culture that is inclusive, equitable, transparent, and respectful of all backgrounds and identities.

Board Relations

* Support the board in recruiting and identifying prospective members who bring diverse skills, perspectives, and strong commitment to Aunt Lute’s mission.
* Maintaining regular communication with the Board Chair through regular check\-ins, and attending and supporting preparation for Board meetings, held every other month to advance organizational priorities and implement strategic planning.
* Providing leadership in developing program, organizational, and financial plans with the Board.

**Required Skills for this Position:**

Required skills and qualifications:

* 3 or more years in non\-profit organizational management within publishing, literary arts, or cultural organizations
* 3 years of experience in managing budgets; considerable experience working with spreadsheets (Microsoft Excel)
* Experience in grant writing, fundraising, and donor relations
* Demonstrated commitment to equitable and transparent collaboration with colleagues
* Highly competent in verbal, written, and visual communication
* Proximity to or ability to commute to the Bay Area for in\-person meetings and events

Preferred skills and qualifications:

* Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors
* Experience with fundraising tech platforms
* Knowledgeable with Social Media and Publicity
* Experience with QuickBooks

**Compensation:**

* $34\-$38/hour for 20 hours per week

**How to Apply:** 

Email a resume and cover letter addressed to Aunt Lute Search Committee to jobs@auntlute.com*.* 

Cover letters should address how applicants believe their qualifications, experience, aspirations, and values align with Aunt Lute’s publishing mission. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and applications will be accepted until the position is filled. If selected for an interview, candidates will be asked to complete an online questionnaire and provide references.

**\*Addendum**

**The Co\-Executive Director in Operations is responsible for:**

* Accounts payable, receivable, banking, and account reconciliation
* Working with the accountant on account reconciliation and end of the year reporting.
* Reporting to the accountant as they close the financial year: on payroll, inventory, sales, etc.
* Payroll and related financial reporting
* Book inventory management, reprints, and shipping
* Serving as liaison with Aunt Lute’s distributor, Ingram
* Overseeing royalty calculations
* Coordinating logistics for book fairs, events, and conferences
* Reporting to the Board on forthcoming book releases, sales, cash and investments, and other operational matter

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy and Development
jobs.description:
**About Rancho Cielo**

Rancho Cielo is a non\-profit organization dedicated to transforming the lives of underserved and at\-risk youth by providing education, vocational training, counseling, and life skills development. In partnership with John Muir Charter School, we support students in earning their high school diploma while preparing them for success in their careers and lives.

**Position Summary**

Rancho Cielo is seeking a strategic, relationship\-driven Director of Philanthropy and Development to lead and grow the organization’s major gifts, planned giving, endowment, and capital funding efforts. This role is responsible for building strong relationships with high\-capacity donors, developing long\-term giving strategies, and securing significant and multi\-year gifts that support the organization’s long\-term financial sustainability and growth.

The Director of Philanthropy and Development will partner closely with the Chief Executive Officer to identify, cultivate, and steward major donors and will work in collaboration with the Chief Financial Officer on endowment growth, capital project funding, and long\-term revenue strategy.

This position focuses on major donors and long\-term funding, while working collaboratively with Development, Marketing, and Grants to ensure a coordinated and effective fundraising strategy.

**Employment Classification: Full\-Time/Exempt**

**Reporting Structure**

· Reports directly to the Chief Executive Officer

· Works closely with the Chief Financial Officer on financial strategy, endowment growth, and long\-term funding.

· Collaborates with Development, Marketing, and Grants teams

**Direct Reports**

· Annual Gifts Manager

**Key Responsibilities**

**Major Gifts \& Donor Strategy**

* Manage a portfolio of high\-capacity donors and prospects
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major gifts
* Develop tailored donor strategies and gift proposals
* Conduct donor meetings and presentations in partnership with the CEO
* Build and manage a strong pipeline of major gift prospects
* Increase average gift size and multi\-year commitment

**Planned Giving \& Endowment**

· Develop and implement a planned giving program

· Promote legacy giving opportunities (bequests, beneficiary designations, trusts, IRA gifts)

· Establish and grow a Legacy Society

· Partner with donors and advisors on planned gift strategies

· Work with Finance to support endowment growth and long\-term funding strategies

**Capital Projects \& Naming Opportunities**

· Identify and cultivate donors for capital projects

· Develop and present naming opportunities

· Structure multi\-year pledges and capital gifts

· Support fundraising efforts tied to campus improvements and program expansion

**CEO \& Leadership Partnership**

· Identify and prepare high\-capacity donor opportunities for the CEO

· Develop briefing materials and donor strategies

· Coordinate donor meetings, follow\-ups, and stewardship activities

· Support the CEO in closing major and transformational gifts

**Fundraising Strategy \& Collaboration**

· Contribute to overall fundraising strategy and donor pipeline development

· Establish goals, metrics, and accountability for major gifts and planned giving

· Collaborate with:

* Development (events, sponsorships, annual giving)
* Marketing (communications, donor messaging)
* Grants (foundation strategy)
* Finance (endowment, pledge tracking, financial planning)
* Strengthen donor stewardship practices and fundraising processes

**Financial \& Strategic Alignment (with CFO)**

* Collaborate on:
* Endowment growth strategy
* Major gift agreements and pledge structures
* Multi\-year revenue forecasting
* Capital project funding strategies
* Naming opportunities and financial modeling
* Ensure alignment between fundraising strategy and financial sustainability goals

**Qualifications**

* 7–15\+ years of experience in nonprofit fundraising, major gifts, or philanthropy
* Proven track record of securing major gifts
* Experience with planned giving, endowment, or capital campaigns preferred
* Strong relationship\-building and donor engagement skills
* Experience working with senior leadership and/or boards
* Strategic thinker with ability to build and grow programs
* Excellent communication and presentation skills
* Experience with donor CRM systems
* Bachelor’s degree required; CFRE or advanced degree preferred

**Key Performance Indicators (KPIS)**

* Major gift revenue
* Planned giving commitments
* Endowment growth contributions
* Number of donor meetings and proposals
* Multi\-year pledges secured
* Growth of major donor pipeline
* Legacy Society participation
* Capital project funding secured
* Contribution to overall fundraising strategy and revenue growth

**First Year Priorities**

* Assess current donor base and identify major gift opportunities
* Build and manage a major donor portfolio
* Launch or expand planned giving / Legacy Society program
* Identify capital project funding opportunities and naming strategies
* Develop donor pipeline, strategy, and reporting metrics
* Establish strong partnership with CEO, CFO, and Development team
* Increase major donor engagement and gift activity

**Compensation Range**: $110,000 \- $130,000

**Work Environment:** This position operates primarily in a professional office environment with frequent interaction with staff, donors, community partners, and board members. This role may require attendance at meetings, fundraising events, and off\-site functions in the evenings or on weekends. Occasional local travel is required for donor visits, community outreach, and organizational events.

jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

The Wealth Client Specialist is a sophisticated wealth expert that focuses on holistically addressing the wealth needs of High Net Worth and Ultra High Net Worth individuals and institutions. This individual has extensive experience in wealth management and effectively introduces appropriate JPMorgan Chase wealth services to best meet the objectives of each client. The Client Specialist provides high level advice and counsel, offers attractive wealth management solutions, and delivers a high level of service.


As a **Wealth Client Specialist within J.P. Morgan Wealth Management**, you will focus on addressing the wealth needs of High Net Worth and Ultra High Net Worth team members and institutions. You will market and sell JPMorgan Chase wealth management services, source new business, and collaborate with a team of professionals to provide high level advice and counsel. You will also keep abreast of trends and strategies in wealth management and engage with other advisors on client engagement efforts. This role requires an autonomous, sophisticated wealth expert who will focus on creating new and deepening existing wealth relationships with high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients across JP Morgan Wealth Management. You will address clients' wealth considerations, collaborate with colleagues to provide high level advice and counsel, market and sell wealth management services, and ensure we have a holistic view of clients' wealth and planning needs.


Your new business generation will come from three primary sources:


* Bank\-referred opportunities
* Existing wealth clients
* Your own business development efforts

In partnership with wealth advisors and private client bankers, you will uncover opportunities with existing and prospective high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients. Your focus will be generating new business. You will not have a “book” of clients or ongoing relationship management responsibilities.


**Job Responsibilities**


* Collaborate with bankers to identify and prioritize opportunities for new wealth relationships
* Engage with Wealth Advisors on deepening existing wealth relationships
* Deliver initial wealth management counsel to prospects and clients recommend customized wealth solutions and the right team to serve their needs
* Generate new assets under management through a focused sales process
* Keep abreast of trends and strategies in wealth management

**Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Series 7, 63, and 65 and insurance licensed
* College graduate with 7\+ years of industry experience
* Proven ability to effectively market and sell wealth management products and services to high net worth and ultra\-high net worth clients
* A sound knowledge base of investing, trust and estates, financial planning, insurance, alternative investments, family wealth, tax considerations, and other related areas
* A self\-confident, proactive professional with the maturity necessary to work autonomously and with people of all levels in the organization
* Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills

**Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills**

* Advanced Degree Preferred
* CFP or CFA designation a plus

This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase's review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
We are hiring an Executive Director who is accountable for the diligent planning, organizing, and energizing of staff, services, and programs to foster a vibrant environment for residents. Ensures strict adherence to regulations concerning resident care, safety, and rights protection. Key responsibilities encompass personnel oversight, culture cultivation, effective communication strategies, financial stewardship, admissions processes, operational best practices, strategic planning, administration, and rigorous quality assurance measures. Will act as the licensed nursing home administrator or delegate under the Administrator's guidance.
What You Will Do:* Works collaboratively with Sequoia Living Support Services (Home Office) and other CCRC/LifePlan locations to identify and implement best practices, unifying where able across all locations.
* Leads and cultivates a positive culture where staff and residents are encouraged to respectfully identify ways we can improve while exhibiting the values of accountability, caring, and teamwork.
* Establishes goals and objectives consistent with mission statements and corporate goals, objectives, and policies. Assures that plans and actions reflect board goals and objectives.
* Develops long term plans, including operation plans, capital plans, major projects, improvements, staffing needs, programs and services.
* Responsible for implementing appropriate corporate policy; makes recommendations for new policies and procedures with staff.
* Performs duties related to staffing including recruiting, screening, hiring, training, orientation, development, evaluation, and motivation of employees.
* Implements plans to achieve performance indicators and dashboard targets.
* Manages the financials including budget development and analysis, administration and forecasting.
* Collaborates with resident leadership and related committees to ensure smooth implementation of community goals and positive resident relations.
* Member of the senior management team. Participates at the corporate level in task forces and committees as required or assigned.
* Serves as Community Risk Manager, overseeing loss prevention and control activities for the entire community under the auspices of the Corporate Risk Management Program.
* Responsible for implementing Safety, Accident and Illness Prevention Program at site. Coordinates Safety Committee.
* Maintains liaison with government agencies, service agencies, neighborhood committees, volunteers, and other professional and supervisory staff.
* Participates in staff development for future continuity and succession planning.
* Performs other work as assigned.


Why Work Here:* For individuals who work more than 30 hrs/week, employer\-paid medical, dental \& vision, 18 days PTO \+ 8 holidays, 403(b) with employer contribution, tuition assistance, referral bonuses, employee discounts, and growth opportunities.


Who You Are:
* Knowledge of Title 22, OBRA and policies and procedures related to the operation of skilled nursing home facilities, intermediate care facilities and residential facilities for the elderly. Management skills to select, train, motivate and develop staff. Skills to develop and maintain interpersonal relationships. Knowledge of the CCRC statutes. Sensitivity and understanding of the issues related to aging. Ability to make sound business decisions. Skill to synthesize a variety of information, consider alternatives and their consequences, formulate conclusions and recommend and implement actions. Sound budgeting development and implementation.
* Eight to ten years of major administrative experience and effective leadership of diverse team members. Previous experience in a similar senior living role. May be required to have or secure a license as a Nursing Home Administrator in California and a Residential Care Facility for the Elderly Certification.
* Full management responsibility for all staff (75 to 175\) activities. Manages directly or through subordinate supervisors. Responsible for recruitment, selection, training, motivation, discipline, and performance appraisal.


Who We Are:
Founded in 1958, Sequoia Living is a Bay Area\-based nonprofit organization dedicated to providing older adults with stimulating, joyful living environments and services that support and enrich their lives. Throughout our six decades as a nonprofit serving Bay Area seniors, we’ve learned the importance of connection and collaboration when it comes to providing resources for healthy aging. From our Life Plan Community to safe affordable housing, engaging senior centers, and a purpose\-filled volunteer program, we provide friendly environments where people can explore and discover what it means to grow stronger, wiser, and more joyful.  

Sequoia Living is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Sequoia Living will provide reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities and encourage prospective employees to discuss potential accommodations with the employer.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

We are seeking an energetic, exceptional Chief Operating Officer to oversee the day\-to\-day operations of our complexes throughout the United States and help drive the company’s continued growth and success. Reporting directly to Ownership, the COO will translate strategy into disciplined execution, strengthen operational systems and leadership capacity, and ensure the organization operates safely, efficiently, and cost\-effectively.

**Key Responsibilities**

· **Set enterprise production standards:** Establish clear expectations for production, cost, quality, safety, delivery, and operational discipline across all complexes.

· **Direct daily operational execution:** Set priorities, allocate resources, approve operating plans, resolve execution issues, and ensure leadership teams operate with urgency and discipline.

· **Drive accountability:** Hold leaders and teams accountable for schedules, cost targets, production goals, quality standards, safety performance, and delivery commitments. Establish clear performance expectations, address issues promptly, and take corrective action through coaching, restructuring, or personnel decisions when required.

· **Intervene decisively:** Act quickly when performance, discipline, or results deviate from expectations by directing corrective actions, changing operating approaches, or making leadership changes necessary to restore performance.

· **Provide enterprise leadership and governance:** Define standards, facilitate cross\-regional alignment, challenge assumptions, and ensure transparent performance reporting.

· **Build senior\-level alignment:** Maintain strong working relationships with Vice Presidents, Production Managers, and their leadership teams to balance business\-unit, regional, and enterprise priorities.

· **Convert strategy into execution:** Turn strategic initiatives into clear plans with defined owners, timelines, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes.

· **Align capital and operations:** Strengthen the connection between strategic objectives, capital deployment, production capacity, capacity planning, improvement initiatives, and approved investment strategies.

· **Deliver executive visibility:** Provide Ownership with clear insight into company operations, project performance, financial trends, organizational capacity, and emerging risks.

· **Advance operational excellence:** Implement and optimize scalable operating systems, management processes, and procedures to improve efficiency, cost\-effectiveness, and execution.

· **Optimize the value chain:** Continuously improve production, sourcing, supply chain, inventory management, fulfillment, logistics, quality, and safety to meet business and customer demands.

· **Lead complex projects:** Oversee expansions, production initiatives, capital projects, and process improvements while strengthening project execution.

· **Support responsible growth:** Partner on business development and growth initiatives while ensuring operational capacity remains aligned with company commitments.

· **Prepare the organization for scale:** Strengthen leadership systems, processes, management depth, and organizational structure to support sustainable long\-term growth.

· **Develop leaders:** Build and lead high\-performing teams; develop future executives, project leaders, and field leaders; and foster collaboration, innovation, inclusion, and alignment with company values and goals.

· **Serve as a trusted operational partner:** Advise Ownership with data\-based analysis, clearly articulated risks, and actionable recommendations, escalating issues when production performance, discipline, or execution falls below agreed standards.

**Candidate Profile**

The successful candidate will be a proven, hands\-on enterprise operator who has built, scaled, and improved complex operations in the food industry. Equally comfortable on the operating floor and in the executive room, this leader will combine strategic judgment, financial acumen, and practical execution. They will make data\-informed decisions, confront underperformance directly, earn credibility with operating leaders, and build the people, systems, and accountability required to scale.

**Qualifications**

· At least 10 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in a complex operational environment.

· A demonstrated record of leading multi\-complex operations and delivering measurable improvements in performance; food\-industry experience is highly desirable.

· Hands\-on command of production, sourcing, supply chain, fulfillment, quality, safety, logistics, and business development.

· Proven ability to build strong leadership teams, develop talent, and lead through accountability and change.

· Exceptional critical\-thinking, problem\-solving, and decision\-making capabilities.

· Working knowledge of human resources and talent\-development practices.

· Executive\-level communication and interpersonal skills, with the credibility to partner effectively with Ownership and senior operational leaders.

· Strong financial acumen and experience managing budgets, resources, cost targets, and operational investments.

· Bachelor’s degree in business administration, management, or a related field.

Physical Demands and working conditions

· Work is normally performed in a typical office work environment. While performing the responsibilities of this position, the individual is required to have ambulatory skills sufficient to visit various parts of the organization.

· Requires the ability to reach with hands and arms, climb stairs and occasionally lift and/or move up to 10lbs.

· Requires sitting and standing for extensive periods of time, operating a computer keyboard, telephone and other equipment for extended periods of time.

· Travel to other facilities throughout the United States and other local travel will be required.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
*Nevada City School of the Arts (NCSOTA), a TK\-8 charter school in operation since 1994, is seeking a dynamic, culturally aware, stimulating and highly qualified Executive Director to join our team.*




**JOB TITLE:** **EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR**

**SCHEDULE:** **2027\-28 School Year – Full\-time**

**WAGE:** **$****125,000 to $166,61****1**




**Nevada City School of the Arts \- Executive Director Job Posting**


Nevada City School of the Arts is seeking an experienced, mission driven leader to serve as its next Executive Director.

**About NCSA**
--------------


Nevada City School of the Arts is a tuition\-free public charter school in California, providing students, families, and staff with an arts based choice for elementary education. NCSA fosters academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement, serves as a collaborator and contributor to the greater community, and is committed to safe, respectful, and equitable conditions for learning and working for everyone in our community.


NCSA is located in Nevada City in the Sierra Nevada foothills, a small, arts rich community with a strong sense of place and civic involvement.

**Enrollment and grades served:** TK\-8, 517 students

**Staff:** 108

**The Position**
----------------


The NCSA Board of Directors, Charter Governance Council, is seeking a highly qualified and dedicated Executive Director to lead Nevada City School of the Arts and advance its mission and vision.


The Executive Director serves as NCSA's chief executive and provides strategic, instructional, organizational, fiscal, personnel, and facilities leadership. The position is responsible for supporting academic excellence, arts integration, student well being, an inclusive and collaborative school culture, and the continued growth and success of NCSA.


The role also includes executive oversight and long term stewardship of NCSA's school owned campus and facilities, including facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, and major projects.

**The Leader We Are Looking For**
---------------------------------


NCSA is seeking an experienced educational and organizational leader who understands the unique character of an arts integrated charter school and can provide strong leadership while preserving and strengthening the qualities that make NCSA special.


The successful candidate will demonstrate:

* A strong commitment to NCSA's mission, vision, and arts integrated educational philosophy.
* A successful record of educational and organizational leadership.
* Experience leading teachers, administrators, classified employees, and other professionals in a school setting.
* Strong instructional leadership and a commitment to academic, artistic, and social emotional achievement.
* Strong financial management skills, including budgeting, forecasting, resource allocation, and long term planning.
* The ability to lead a complex organization, establish priorities, delegate effectively, develop strong teams, and follow through.
* Experience overseeing complex facilities, long term facilities planning, deferred maintenance, capital improvements, or comparable organizational assets.
* The ability to navigate difficult issues, manage competing priorities, build consensus, and lead an organization through change.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills and the ability to build relationships with students, staff, families, the Board, and the broader community.
* Integrity, sound judgment, humility, curiosity, collaboration, and a commitment to continued professional growth.

**Board and Governance Relationship**
-------------------------------------


The Executive Director reports to the Charter Governance Council and is expected to understand and respect the distinction between Board governance and Executive Director management.


The successful candidate will be comfortable operating independently within authority delegated by the Board while communicating openly and proactively and providing clear, timely information necessary for effective Board oversight.


NCSA's Board operates under the Carver Model of Governance, also known as Policy Governance, in which the Board establishes organizational Ends and Executive Limitations, monitors organizational performance, and speaks with one voice, while delegating authority to the Executive Director to manage operations within those established boundaries.

**Why NCSA**
------------


NCSA is sponsored by the Nevada County Board of Education. Beyond the school itself, Nevada County is a wonderful place to call home \- year\-round outdoor and community activities, and a vibrant, deeply rooted arts and cultural scene.

jobs.description:
**Chief Operating Officer (COO)**

**Position Overview**


Farahi Law Firm is an award\-winning personal injury firm dedicated to fighting for the injured and delivering exceptional legal representation. We are a fast\-growing, client\-centric team that values aggressive advocacy, innovation, and community impact. We're seeking a high\-performing COO with deep operational experience inside a personal injury law firm. You will act as the second\-in\-command to the CEO and run the daily operations of a multi\-department law firm with 200\+ staff, 19 departments, and aggressive growth goals. This is not a learning position — it's for someone who has already operated in the trenches of personal injury and knows how to make every part of the engine run efficiently.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Departmental Oversight**

* Direct, lead, and optimize daily operations across Intake, Case Management, Pre\-Lit, Lit, Medical Records, Negotiations, Investigations, and Client Experience.
* Ensure KPI tracking, data visibility, and accountability in each department.

**Process \& Systems Leadership**

* Lead firm\-wide process mapping, SOP creation, and cross\-functional system alignment (Lead Docket, Filevine, RingCentral, CallRail, G Suite).
* Optimize workflow automation and collaboration between Intake, CM, and Medical teams.

**People Management \& Performance**

* Hire, onboard, and coach department leads and hold them to performance\-based metrics.
* Establish structured onboarding, cross\-training, and succession planning systems.

**Medical \& Vendor Negotiation**

* Lead medical provider negotiations, lien reductions, and ensure client medical management is cost\-effective and streamlined.
* Manage investigation resources, vendor contracts, and vendor KPI evaluation.

**Operational Reporting \& Decision Support**

* Build dashboards in Looker Studio, track progress against KPIs, and support the CEO in decision\-making.
* Present weekly scorecards across departments and identify areas of underperformance.

**Requirements \& Qualifications**

* 7\+ years as COO or Director of Operations in a personal injury law firm.
* Deep knowledge of intakes, case management, litigation, medical records, and investigations.
* Experience with KPIs, process mapping, and automation tools.
* Prior ownership of law firm P\&L, budgeting, and staffing plans.
* Skilled in medical negotiations, lien reductions, and cost control.
* High emotional intelligence with zero micromanagement needed.
* Strong technical understanding of law firm tech stacks (Filevine, Lead Docket, G Suite, RingCentral, etc.).

**What Success Looks Like**

* 90%\+ of department KPIs hit consistently; increased case velocity without reducing settlement value.
* Meaningful reduction in medical spend per case through better negotiation; investigations completed in under 3 days per case.
* High team engagement, low turnover, and a clear org chart with successors in place; CEO involvement in day\-to\-day ops reduced by 75%.

**Soft Skills \& Personality Fit**

* Strategic operator with a bias for action who can teach others, not just do the work.
* Calm under pressure, direct communicator who holds teams accountable while building morale.
* Operates with a CEO mindset and owner mentality.

**Job Title:** Executive Director


**Location:** Remote with occasional regional and national travel. Candidate must reside in one of the six New England States (CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT)


**Position Type:** Full\-Time

  


**Summary of position:**


*The Baker Center for Children and Families (also known as Judge Baker Children's Center), promotes the best possible mental health of children and families through the integration of research, intervention, training, and policy.*

  



The New England Association of Child Welfare Commissioners and Directors (NEACWCD), housed at the Baker Center for Children and Families, is seeking an experienced, collaborative leader to serve as its next Executive Director.

  



NEACWCD is a member organization comprised of the six public child welfare agencies serving Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Vermont. For nearly 40 years, the Association has brought child welfare leaders together to learn from one another, solve shared challenges, and advance innovative policy and practice through collaborative initiatives, research, strategic partnerships, and peer learning.

  



The Executive Director serves as a trusted advisor, facilitator, and connector for Commissioners and Directors across the region. This is a unique opportunity for a leader who enjoys bringing people together, building relationships across systems, identifying emerging opportunities, and turning ideas into meaningful regional work. The Executive Director also connects New England leaders with emerging research, promising practices, national experts, and technical assistance resources. Current priorities include advancing a kin\-first culture and support for kinship caregivers; promoting authentic engagement of youth and families with lived experience; and fostering cross\-state collaboration related to permanency, workforce development, and child welfare outcomes. These priorities will continue to evolve in partnership with NEACWCD's members. The incoming Executive Director will join NEACWCD during a planned leadership transition and will have the opportunity to work alongside the current Executive Director for a period of onboarding and relationship transition.

  


**Why This Role Is Different**

NEACWCD is not a traditional direct\-service organization. Its members are the six public child welfare agencies of New England, and the Executive Director's role is to help those leaders accomplish together what may be difficult to accomplish alone.  



The position offers unusual access to state and national child welfare leadership and the opportunity to shape regional initiatives, bring new ideas and resources into New England, and build partnerships that strengthen policy and practice across state lines.  



NEACWCD is a small organization with a large reach. The Executive Director must be equally comfortable thinking strategically with Commissioners and national partners, facilitating a multi\-state conversation, developing a new initiative, managing a grant or budget, and attending to the practical details necessary to move the work forward.  


**Essential duties****:**


* Builds trusted relationships with Commissioners, Directors, and other senior child welfare leaders across the six New England states.

* Oversees the Association's finances, contracts, operations, grants, and organizational sustainability.
* Represents NEACWCD in regional and national initiatives and conferences.

**Executive Director**

Mount Sopris Montessori School \| Carbondale, Colorado

In\-person \| Full\-time \| Salaried, exempt

**Salary range: $90,000–$130,000 annually**

About Us

Located on a quiet residential street in the beautiful mountain town of Carbondale, Colorado, Mount Sopris Montessori School is a nonprofit preschool serving about 60 children ages 18 months through 6 years. Founded in 1981 by Kathryn and Mark Ross, the not\-for\-profit school is recognized as an exceptional preschool environment, based on the Montessori Method of child\-led learning. The school offers dedicated preschool and toddler classrooms led by experienced educators, with teachers certified through organizations such as the American Montessori Society (AMS), American Montessori International (AMI), or the North American Montessori Center (NAMC).

Position Summary

We seek a director who recognizes the critical importance of an inspired preschool education. Preschool is a critical educational period because roughly 90% of a child’s brain development happens before age five, laying the foundational cognitive, social, and emotional habits for life.

The Executive Director provides strategic, financial, and organizational leadership for Mount Sopris Montessori School. The Executive Director sets direction in partnership with the Board of Directors, holds ultimate accountability for the school's financial health and regulatory standing, and leads the Assistant Director and staff in delivering a high\-quality Montessori program. Montessori training is provided as part of onboarding.

*This role reports to the Board of Directors (via the Board President) and directly supervises the Assistant Director, who manages day\-to\-day school operations. This is a Colorado Department of Early Childhood (CDEC) “Director of Record” position — the Executive Director carries ultimate licensing accountability for the center.*

Key Responsibilities

**Governance \& Strategy**

* Partner with the Board to set and execute annual and multi\-year strategic plan and priorities.
* Translate Board\-approved strategy into operational goals for the Assistant Director and staff.
* Attend Board meetings, report on enrollment, finances, program quality, and compliance.
* Identify risks and opportunities affecting the school's long\-term sustainability.

**Family \& Enrollment Relations**

* Manage the admissions pipeline: tours, applications, and family onboarding.
* Monitor enrollment and retention by classroom; flag enrollment risks early.

**Financial Management \& Fundraising**

* Develop and manage the annual budget in partnership with the Board and bookkeeper.
* Monitor tuition revenue, staffing costs, and cash flow against budget.
* Oversee participation in and compliance with public funding and support programs, including CCCAP, UPK, Colorado Shines, and other local, state, and federal programs to maximize funding.
* Proactively identify and pursue funding opportunities for which the school is eligible.
* Lead fundraising and development: annual giving, donor relationships, grants, and events.

**Organizational \& Staff Leadership**

* Hire, onboard, and evaluate the Assistant Director and lead teaching staff.
* Coach and mentor teachers on curriculum implementation and classroom practices.
* Set compensation, handle disciplinary matters, and maintain employee handbook policies.
* Build and maintain a healthy, mission\-aligned staff culture.

**Facilities Oversight \& Management**

* Identify and plan for capital improvements and major facility expenditures in partnership with the Board.
* Develop a long\-term strategic plan for the school's grounds and physical campus as a core asset.

**Licensing, Compliance \& Community**

* Maintain staff qualifications, background checks, and training records for CDEC compliance.
* Represent the school within the Carbondale and Roaring Fork Valley community.
* Set enrollment strategy and monitor overall enrollment against budget.
* Champion the school's Montessori philosophy and educational quality standards.

Required Qualifications

* College Degree (Bachelor’s degree in early childhood education or similar)
* Qualifies as Director under current CDEC requirements for a Large Child Care Center (or can obtain CDEC Director qualification verification before start).
* Senior leadership or Board\-level experience in a school, nonprofit, or comparable organization.
* Budget development and financial management experience.
* Fundraising, development, or donor relations experience.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through organizational change.
* Sound judgment handling confidential and sensitive matters.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master's degree in early childhood education, educational leadership, or administration
* Experience in a Montessori school or familiarity with Montessori philosophy.
* Experience directing a licensed Colorado child\-care center.
* Nonprofit governance experience.

Schedule

Full\-time, in\-person, Monday–Friday during school operating hours, with occasional evenings or weekends for Board meetings and school events.

Benefits

* Simple IRA with a match of up to 3% of salary
* Modest Health Insurance Stipend

How to Apply

Submit a resume, a brief letter of interest, and your current CDEC Director qualification status to hiring@mtsoprismontessori.com. Employment is contingent on verification of qualifications, background checks, and references.

Mount Sopris Montessori School is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome qualified applicants and do not discriminate based on any status protected by applicable law.

The 1932 Criterion Theatre brings the Mount Desert Island community together through distinctive performing arts and cultural programming. We champion creativity while preserving our historic venue for the enjoyment and enrichment of current and future generations.

The Director of Development is a key member of the Theatre's leadership team, responsible for the strategic and day\-to\-day oversight of the organization's fundraising program, including sponsorships, individual giving, foundation and grant relationships, the annual appeal, and special events. This position plays a vital role in advancing the organization's mission by building and sustaining the relationships and revenue that make the Theatre's programming possible. As a member of a small, collaborative team, you will take on a broad range of responsibilities across multiple functions. This role is well suited to a versatile professional who values variety, adapts readily to shifting priorities, and is comfortable working independently.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:***Development Strategy* 

In partnership with the Executive Director, the Director of Development executes a comprehensive development strategy encompassing sponsorship, individual giving, foundation support, the annual appeal, and special events, setting and tracking fundraising goals. They help foster a collaborative, respectful, mission\-driven approach to donor engagement across the organization.

*Corporate \& Business Sponsorship*

Cultivates, solicits, and stewards relationships with corporate and business sponsors, developing sponsorship packages and benefits tied to performances and seasonal programming, and ensuring sponsor benefits and recognition are fulfilled on time.

Builds and manages a donor pipeline from first\-time givers to major donors, developing personalized cultivation and stewardship plans for key supporters, and maintaining accurate donor records and giving history. *Foundation \& Grant Relations*

This includes researching and cultivating relationships with foundations and grant\-making institutions, preparing compelling grant proposals and reports, and tracking application deadlines and compliance requirements.

About Evergreen Goodwill
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill of Northwest Washington is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization founded in 1923 that helps people get jobs across Northwest Washington by offering high\-quality free job training, education and job placement. Goodwill empowers individuals to overcome barriers to working, by providing comprehensive support and connecting them with life changing job opportunities, ensuring they are career\-ready and can support themselves and their families.
  
  

The organization employs over 2,000 people, operates five job\-training centers, 23 nonprofit retail stores and more than 27 donation sites in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom and Kitsap Counties. Every day, Evergreen Goodwill connects people with the jobs, services and skills they need — because Jobs Change Lives. We are committed to creating and sustaining a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion (DEI) and are focused on creating a joyful, inclusive and successful organization.
  
  

**Job Title:** Executive Director, Evergreen Goodwill Education Center
  
**Location:** Evergreen Goodwill Job Training \& Education Center \- Seattle, WA
  
**Salary Range:** $180,000–$220,000
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill is seeking a Founding Executive Director to build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center (EGEC), a new organization formed to operate Washington State’s first adult high school using the Goodwill Education Initiatives model. Over the next decade, the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center plans to launch at least five Excel Centers—public high schools for adults ages 18 and older—in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom, and Kitsap counties. Washington’s Excel Centers will build on the national Goodwill Excel Center model, which now includes 50 campuses across 11 states and Washington, D.C. The model combines rigorous academics, wraparound services, and life coaching to help adult students earn high school diplomas.
  
The Executive Director will shape the execution strategy, build the organization, launch its schools, beginning with Excel Center Goodwill Dearborn in Seattle, and lead them toward long\-term success.
  
We are looking for an executive and builder who can define a bold strategy, translate it into action, and deliver on the promise of these schools. This leader will build and inspire a team, deliver strong student outcomes, engage funders and community partners, advocate for the schools, build an effective board and collaborate with its members, and create a financially and operationally sustainable institution.
  
About The Excel Center
  
The Excel Center model is a tuition\-free public high school designed to help adults earn a state\-recognized diploma, not a GED, along with college credits or industry certifications. Flexible schedules, life coaching, childcare, and transportation support help students balance school with work and family responsibilities. Excel Center graduates earn more than a diploma: they gain college credits and professional certifications that open doors to higher\-paying careers in high\-growth fields. A University of Notre Dame LEO study of the Excel Center model in Indiana found that, five years after graduation, graduates earn 38% more and are significantly more likely to work in fields with career pathways, such as healthcare.
  
Evergreen Goodwill will bring the model to Washington and build on it. We aspire to open an Excel Center in each of the five counties where we operate, ultimately reaching 1,000–1,500 students within the next decade. The founding Executive Director will benefit from a proven model and significant training, guidance, and ongoing support from Goodwill Education Initiatives (GEI), the national experts behind The Excel Center, while shaping the school to meet the needs of our local community. A combination of public funding, including charter school funding, and private philanthropy will support the school.
  
**Learn more about the national Excel Center model:** https://www.goodwillexcelcenter.org/
  
  

**Five key functions of this role include:**  

1\. Academic Excellence, Curriculum Oversight, and Student Outcomes
  
2\. Culture, Talent, and Organizational Leadership
  
3\. Student Recruitment, Enrollment and Retention
  
4\. Partnerships, Board Engagement, Fundraising, and External Leadership
  
5\. Financial Management, Compliance and Accountability
  
What You’ll Do
  
* Build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center organization. You’ll hire and supervise the Excel Center principals and help build a team that includes teachers, special education and language teachers, coaches, a registrar, and an office manager. You’ll build the school culture, academic program, operations, systems, and infrastructure and put strong academic leadership and expertise in place to support the educational program.
* Shape the operational and growth strategy for the Excel Centers in Washington, translating a proven national model into exceptional public high schools for adults ages 18 and older that are responsive to their local communities.
* Set ambitious goals for enrollment, persistence, graduation, and postsecondary success, using data and accountability to drive strong student outcomes.
* Ensure the financial and operational health of the organization and its schools by overseeing budgeting, staffing, resource allocation, accreditation, charter requirements, and regulatory compliance.
* Serve as the external leader for the Excel Centers, building strong relationships with the board, funders, employers, colleges, community organizations, public leaders, and other partners while leading fundraising, advocacy, and policy engagement for the schools.
* Build a sustainable institution with the visibility, partnerships, funding, and organizational strength to deepen its impact and support expansion across the five counties Evergreen Goodwill serves.

**Director of Major Gifts**

**Charleston School of Law**

**Position Summary**


Charleston School of Law seeks a highly relational, community\-minded professional to serve as its Director of Major Gifts. This position will play an important role in expanding the school's relationships throughout Charleston, the Lowcountry, Statewide and Nationally while developing those relationships into meaningful philanthropic support for the school and its students.


The Director of Major Gifts will identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward individuals and organizations with the interest and capacity to make significant investments in Charleston School of Law. The successful candidate will be a natural relationship builder who enjoys meeting people, making connections, developing trust, and representing an organization within the community and beyond.


While previous fundraising experience is valuable, it is not required. Successful candidates may come from advancement, business development, sales, law, banking and financial services, professional services, community relations, nonprofit leadership, hospitality, civic engagement, or other relationship\-centered fields.


Of particular importance is an understanding of Charleston, the Lowcountry and South Carolina, and the ability to build authentic relationships with alumni, attorneys, business and civic leaders, community partners, corporations, foundations, and friends of the school.


The Director of Major Gifts will work closely with the School's Advancement team and senior leadership to expand the school's network, strengthen existing relationships, identify new prospective donors and partners, and generate philanthropic support for scholarships, academic programs, faculty excellence, student opportunities, strategic initiatives, and other institutional priorities.

* Work with School leadership, faculty, alumni, Board members, and other volunteers to facilitate introductions and develop donor relationships.
* Maintain appropriate follow\-up and stewardship following gifts and significant donor interactions.


Community, Donor, and Alumni Engagement

* Serve as a visible and effective ambassador for Charleston School of Law throughout Charleston, the Lowcountry and South Carolina.
* Develop and strengthen relationships with alumni, attorneys, business and civic leaders, community organizations, corporations, foundations, and friends of the school.
* Expand the school's network within the Charleston community and identify opportunities to introduce new individuals and organizations to the school.
* Attend community, professional, alumni, donor, and School events as appropriate to build relationships and increase the school's visibility.
* Build long\-term relationships based on trust, engagement, and a genuine understanding of the interests of prospective donors and partners.

* Assist in developing opportunities for donors, alumni, and community leaders to become more engaged with the school.


Strategic Development

* Work collaboratively with the Advancement team and School leadership to establish annual and long\-term fundraising priorities and strategies.
* Help develop a sustainable pipeline of prospective donors and move relationships from initial introduction through cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* Support fundraising efforts related to scholarships, academic programs, student opportunities, special initiatives, capital priorities, and other institutional needs.
* Bring forward ideas for new partnerships, relationships, sponsorships, and philanthropic opportunities based on knowledge of the Charleston and Lowcountry communities.
* Help identify emerging opportunities for the school to strengthen its relationships with the legal, business, civic, nonprofit, and philanthropic communities.
* Establish measurable relationship\-development and fundraising goals and provide regular updates regarding progress.

* Track prospective donors and opportunities and ensure appropriate and timely follow\-up.

What starts here changes the world.

  

The University of Texas at Austin, founded in 1883, ranks among the best universities in the world. With 76 programs ranked in the top 10, UT Austin is the \#1 public university in Texas and the \#7 public university in the nation.

jobs.description:
### About Us:


The DC History Center and HumanitiesDC recently announced that they intend to merge. This fall, we will become a single nonprofit dedicated to preserving the District’s history, celebrating its culture, and supporting the humanities. From our base at the Carnegie Library, DC History Center \+ HumanitiesDC will offer research, education, grants, and programming opportunities to match any level of knowledge or interest in the District. Our new organization will be a place for DC’s curious minds to build community, find common ground, and help shape the future of our nation’s capital.

### Position Summary:


DC History Center \+ HumanitiesDC is seeking a strategic, energetic, and mission\-driven Director of Development and Communications to lead our fundraising, communications, and marketing efforts. As a member of the Leadership Team, you will partner closely with the Executive Director to shape organizational strategy, grow philanthropic support, and elevate our voice in the community.


You'll lead a talented Development and Communications Team, supervising three direct\-reports while managing a departmental budget, a major gifts portfolio, and the organization's brand and media presence. This role requires a Monday–Friday schedule with regular evening and weekend commitments for organizational events.

### Responsibilities:


Strategy, Vision \& Leadership

* Help shape organizational strategy and annual fundraising and communications plans
* Advise the Executive Director on fundraising and communications
* Manage the department's annual budget and long\-term goals


Fundraising

* Manage a major gifts portfolio while supporting the organization’s institutional relationships
* Set annual fundraising goals and oversee workflows to achieve them
* Support board fundraising, staff the Development Committee, and help recruit new board members
* Supervise grant writing and guide prospecting for new grant funders and individual donors
* Develop a planned giving program and a stewardship strategy across donor levels
* Supervise annual fund, membership, and events


Communications \& Marketing

* Set strategy for institutional messaging, media relations, and marketing
* Serve as primary media contact and lead the organization's visibility efforts
* Oversee production of the annual report, from content to design and distribution


Community Relations \& Advocacy

* Lead advocacy strategy for the DC humanities sector, particularly with DC government
* Represent the organization externally and with key partners such as DowntownDC BID, Events DC, and DC Public Library


Team Development

* Coach and grow a high\-performing Development and Communications team
* Set staff goals, provide ongoing feedback, and support professional growth

### What You Bring:

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience, plus 7\+ years \[LH5\.1]of experience in fundraising, grant writing, communications, project management, media relations, or marketing – ideally in Washington, DC;
* Experience\[LH6\.1] creating and stewarding donor and partner relationships that lead to financial support;
* A track record of leading teams and driving organizational growth and change;
* Experience working across diverse communities;
* Excellent written, oral, and presentation skills, with sharp attention to detail;
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, SharePoint, Teams, and CRMs; familiarity with Adobe Creative Suite and WordPress is a plus;
* Fluency in Spanish, French, Amharic, or Chinese is a plus.

### Compensation:


This role will be paid an annual salary based on our Compensation Framework and Strategy, plus a robust benefits package including medical, dental, and vision insurance, 401K with 4% match, holidays and paid closures, paid leave, short\-and long\-term disability coverage, paid parental leave, pre\-tax SmarTrip contributions, and more. DC History Center \+ HumanitiesDC does not negotiate salaries or benefits at the time of hire or any other time.

### How To Apply:


Please submit a resume and cover letter describing your interest in and qualifications for the role through the Jobscore platform. Candidates are welcome to include up to two short writing samples representative of work products related to the role. Please note that all applications will be reviewed by a human, not an AI screening tool. Additionally, we request that you refrain from using AI to compile your application or indicate where and how it was used if you include AI\-generated content. This posting was created with the assistance of AI.


Please apply by October 18 for the best opportunity to be considered. After October 18, applications will be considered on a rolling basis until the role is filled. The hiring process will include no more than three rounds of interviews. We aim to fill the position by mid\-December.


DC History Center \+ HumanitiesDC is an equal opportunity employer.

**The Children’s House Child Advocacy Center (CHCAC)**  
**Towanda, Pennsylvania**  
**Full\-Time \| Primarily Monday–Friday**

The Children’s House Child Advocacy Center (CHCAC) is seeking a highly motivated, mission\-driven Executive Director to lead our organization into its next chapter.

CHCAC is an independent nonprofit organization dedicated to reducing trauma for children and families impacted by abuse. Through a collaborative, multidisciplinary approach, we provide a safe and supportive environment that promotes healing, justice, and prevention.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the organization’s chief executive and provides leadership for CHCAC’s programs, staff, finances, fundraising, community partnerships, compliance, and long\-term sustainability.

The successful candidate will be a collaborative and strategic leader who can strengthen our organization while maintaining CHCAC’s commitment to providing high\-quality, trauma\-informed services to children and families.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

The Executive Director will:

* Provide organizational leadership and strategic direction in partnership with the Board of Directors
* Lead, supervise, support, and develop CHCAC staff
* Oversee organizational operations, policies, programs, accreditation, and compliance
* Develop and manage the annual budget and maintain strong fiscal controls
* Provide leadership for grant development, administration, compliance, and reporting
* Lead fundraising and development efforts in collaboration with staff, the Board, and community partners
* Build and maintain strong relationships with law enforcement, child protection services, healthcare providers, schools, the District Attorney’s Office, and other community partners
* Support and strengthen CHCAC’s multidisciplinary team (MDT) partnerships
* Represent CHCAC through community outreach, presentations, partnerships, and public communications
* Maintain organizational readiness for state, regional, and National Children’s Alliance accreditation requirements
* Ensure effective risk management, organizational continuity, and long\-term sustainability
* Maintain appropriate training and qualifications to provide backup coverage for key CAC services as organizational needs require

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Required:**

* Bachelor’s degree
* Minimum of five years of progressive leadership experience in nonprofit management, human services, or a related field
* Strong organizational, leadership, written, and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated ability to lead teams and collaborate with multidisciplinary partners
* Valid driver’s license and ability to commute throughout the area and state.

**Preferred:**

* Master’s degree in social work, public administration, nonprofit management, or a related field
* Experience working within a Children’s Advocacy Center, child welfare, law enforcement, victim services, or a related child\-abuse response system
* Knowledge of trauma\-informed practices and child\-abuse service systems
* Experience with grant writing, grant administration, compliance, and reporting
* Experience in fundraising, donor relations, and event management

**BENEFITS**

CHCAC offers a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

* 100% employer\-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for the employee
* 14 paid holidays
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan with up to a 3% company match
* Employee Assistance Program
* Employee wellness initiatives
* Flexible work schedule
* Continuing education and professional development opportunities, including access to state, regional, and national Children’s Advocacy Center training
* Salary commensurate with experience

**MAKE A DIFFERENCE**

This is an opportunity to lead an organization whose work directly impacts children, families, and communities throughout the region.

If you are a compassionate, collaborative, and experienced leader who believes in strengthening the coordinated response to child abuse and building a sustainable organization for the future, we encourage you to apply.

**HOW TO APPLY**

Interested candidates should submit a letter of interest and résumé.

We invite qualified candidates who share our commitment to supporting children and families to apply for this important leadership opportunity.

The Children’s House Child Advocacy Center is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

Pay: $50,000\.00 \- $65,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

**Location:** Schenectady, NY Category: Professional Job Type: Full\-time Posted On: Tue Sep 29 2026 Job Description:
  
  

SUNY Schenectady County Community College seeks applicants for the position of Executive Director, Sponsored Programs. The position will report directly to the College President and be required to provide leadership and oversight for the College's portfolio of grants and sponsored projects, including researching funding opportunities and pursuing and writing competitive proposals for government agencies, foundations, and other sponsors. The Executive Director oversees grant implementation, budgets, performance, reporting, evaluation, and regulatory compliance; provides technical assistance and training on grant requirements and develops standardized processes to support effective grants management and successful project outcomes.
  
  

**Supervisory Responsibility:**  

The Executive Director is responsible for the supervision, direction, and evaluation of grants and sponsored programs staff as assigned. Responsibilities may include hiring, onboarding, training, goal setting, performance management, and professional development of staff supporting grant development, grant administration, sponsored programs, workforce development, community education, and related externally funded initiatives.
  
  

The Executive Director provides leadership through project coordination, collaboration, and consultation with internal and external stakeholders and may oversee additional positions as the College's grants and sponsored programs function expands.
  
  

**Responsibilities:**  

Grant Development and Writing
  
  

Serve as the College's primary grant writer and lead the development of competitive grant proposals.
  
Research, identify, and evaluate potential funding opportunities from federal, state, local, foundation, and corporate sources.
  
Develop and prepare grant narratives, budgets, work plans, implementation strategies, logic models, evaluation plans, and supporting documentation.
  
Coordinate and facilitate grant development activities involving faculty, staff, administrators, and external partners.
  
Establish and maintain a grant opportunity calendar and proposal development schedule.
  
Assist with the review and submission of grant applications to ensure compliance with sponsor and institutional requirements. Actively seeks additional grant funding opportunities to support Presidential initiatives, programs and services, and to compliment the institutional mission.
  
Researches, applies and reports on all grants while communicating to appropriate campus leaders about such grant\-funded opportunities.
  
Reviews literature dealing with funds available through grants from governmental agencies and private foundations to determine feasibility of developing programs to support institutional priorities.
  
Develops and coordinates grant funded programs with agencies, institutions, local government, or units of local government, such as school systems or police departments.
  
Writes grant application, according to format required and in collaboration with others, and submits application in a complete and timely fashion to funding agency or foundation. Meets with appropriate representatives of funding sources to work out final details of proposal.
  
Ensures compliance with grant funds from external sources/agencies
  
Develops and maintain contracts, Memorandum of Agreements and Understanding with local, state and federal funding agencies.
  
Monitors paperwork connected with grant\-funded programs.
  
  

Grant Management and Compliance
  
  

Monitor awarded grants to ensure compliance with funding requirements, reporting obligations, and program objectives.
  
Collaborate with Finance and project personnel regarding budget administration, allowable expenditures, and grant performance metrics.
  
Assist with grant reporting, renewals, amendments, audits, and closeout activities.
  
Maintain accurate records of grant activities, outcomes, and reporting requirements.
  
  

Strategic Planning and Resource Development
  
  

Advise the President and College leadership on emerging funding opportunities, grant trends, and sponsored program initiatives.
  
Prepare reports and analyses regarding grant activity, funding outcomes, and institutional impact.
  
Support the College's strategic priorities by identifying and pursuing external funding opportunities that enhance programs, services, facilities, and student success initiatives.
  
  

Collaboration and Capacity Building
  
  

Develop and deliver grant\-related training, resources, and technical assistance to faculty and staff.
  
Cultivate and maintain collaborative relationships with funding agencies, community organizations, educational partners, and other stakeholders.
  
Promote a culture of grant seeking and resource development across the institution.
  
Perform other related duties as assigned.
  
  

**Job Requirements:**  

**Job Requirements:**  

Demonstrated ability to research, develop, write, and submit successful grant proposals.
  
Strong knowledge of grant funding sources, proposal development processes, and sponsored programs administration.
  
Knowledge of federal, state, foundation, and corporate grant programs and related compliance requirements.
  
Excellent written, verbal, editing, and presentation skills.
  
Strong project management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
  
Ability to analyze information, develop funding strategies, and translate institutional priorities into competitive funding proposals.
  
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with diverse internal and external stakeholders.
  
Strong budget development and financial analysis skills related to grant proposal preparation and administration.
  
Demonstrated initiative, attention to detail, and ability to work independently.
