jobs.title: Director of Operations and Finance
jobs.description:
**Overview**

**Director of Operations and Finance** Job Summary

The Director of Operations and Finance supports the financial and administrative operations of Tennessee Caregiver Coalition. Working closely with the President \& CEO, the Director of Operations and Finance manages grant applications and reporting, coordinates the monthly financial close, processes payroll, and maintains systems that help the organization meet its obligations to staff, funders, and caregivers. This is a hands\-on, part\-time role for someone who can manage deadlines, work accurately with financial information, and identify issues early.

This is a part\-time position based in the Nashville office, with a schedule of 12 hours per week during the hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. During the first three months of employment, all scheduled hours will be worked in the office as part of onboarding. Upon successful completion of this period, the employee will be eligible for a hybrid schedule, with at least one in\-office day per week and additional in\-office time as needed. The specific schedule will be set in consultation with the President \& CEO.

This position has the potential to grow into a full\-time Chief Operating Officer role if additional grant funding is secured and organizational needs support the expansion. Any change in hours, title, or responsibilities would be determined by the Tennessee Caregiver Coalition at that time.

This position includes a six\-month probationary assessment period, with a performance review at 90 days and a final review at the six\-month mark to assess progress, long\-term fit, and success in the role. Continuation in the role is contingent upon meeting established performance standards.

The Tennessee Caregiver Coalition is committed to actively cultivating and preserving a culture of equity, inclusion and connectedness. We strive to create a space that enables everyone to bring their full self to the work and that embraces the full spectrum of humanity. These values permeate all aspects of our work.

We are committed to equitable hiring, training, promotional practices, and policies. We value the unique contributions people bring in terms of education, opinions, culture, ethnicity, race, sex, gender identity and expression, nation of origin, age, languages spoken, veteran’s status, color, marital status, religion, ability, sexual orientation, and beliefs. **We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.**

Key Responsibilities and Measurable Performance Standards

**Agency Culture \& Leadership**

* Maintain a positive, solutions\-focused attitude, ensuring:
* 100% of interactions with staff, volunteers, and partners are respectful, professional, and encouraging
* Concerns and challenges are addressed constructively, with a focus on problem\-solving rather than negativity
* Personal stress and frustrations are managed in a way that does not negatively impact the workplace environment
* Demonstrate commitment to TCC values in action, ensuring:
* Decisions, interactions, and leadership actions align with TCC’s mission and values
* Proactively models agency values in everyday work, including integrity, accountability, and compassion
* Commitment to equity and inclusion, ensuring:
* Actively participates in agency\-wide equity and inclusion efforts
* Addresses bias and inequities within programs and operations in a thoughtful and proactive manner
* Ensures staff, volunteers, and program participants feel valued, respected, and included
* Support a collaborative and morale\-boosting work environment, ensuring:
* Encourages teamwork, open communication, and mutual respect among staff
* Addresses agency morale concerns within two weeks when issues arise
* Recognizes and celebrates staff successes and program achievements regularly
* Attends and contributes positively to all staff meetings and agency discussions

**Grants \& Contracts**

* Maintain a calendar of grant application, reporting, and contract deadlines.
* Research and identify new grant opportunities that align with Tennessee Caregiver Coalition’s mission, programs, and funding priorities.
* Assess eligibility, funding requirements, and organizational capacity; recommend promising opportunities to the CEO.
* Lead the development and submission of new grant applications, working with the CEO and program staff to prepare proposals, budgets, and supporting materials.
* Coordinate and prepare grant applications, budgets, renewals, and required attachments in partnership with the CEO and program staff.
* Prepare grant reports by gathering financial and program information, checking it for completeness, and submitting reports on time.
* Track grant spending and deliverables, and alert the CEO to potential shortfalls, restrictions, or compliance concerns.
* Maintain organized grant and contract records.

**Financial Operations**

* Coordinate the monthly financial close with the bookkeeper or accountant, including reviewing transactions, reconciliations, grant coding, and outstanding items.
* Prepare monthly financial reports and explain significant budget variances to the CEO.
* Monitor accounts receivable, including state reimbursement requests and outstanding payments, and provide regular cash flow updates.
* Review the status of accounts payable and upcoming obligations so the CEO can plan for payroll, voucher reimbursements, and other expenses.
* Help prepare the annual organizational budget and grant budgets.
* Coordinate the information needed for the annual audit or financial review and required financial filings.

**Payroll and Operational Systems** 

* Run payroll accurately and on schedule, including reviewing time records, approved changes, and payroll reports.
* Maintain written procedures and a reliable calendar for recurring financial, payroll, and grant tasks.
* Identify ways to improve accuracy, documentation, and coordination across financial and program systems

**Executive Director \- NW Arkansas** 

As Immerse Arkansas expands into Northwest Arkansas, **we are looking for a strong Executive Director to lead a new site into the next phase of growth and development as well as grow its impact.** We seek a galvanizer, excellent implementer, systems builder, and a healthy leader with a strong entrepreneurial spirit. An effective Executive Director also carries a presence to guide the site’s community engagement, local fundraising, and key relationships with donors and stakeholders.

The Executive Director is responsible for all components of Immerse Arkansas’ development, service delivery, and operations at the Immerse Arkansas site in Northwest Arkansas. This includes overseeing the delivery of supports to youth and families, leading strong and effective teams, ensuring smooth and effective operations, growing the organization’s presence, and implementing the site’s development efforts. This also includes leading the site to achieve a high level of impact in all organizational domains.

**ROLE DESCRIPTION** 

Reporting to the CEO, the Northwest Arkansas Executive Director will:

* Oversee the launch and implementation of Immerse’s model to serve families and youth from crisis in Northwest Arkansas. Cast vision for the site’s future initiatives and community presence in tandem with support from Immerse’s BASE\-Q team.
* Lead the organization’s regional fundraising presence and develop strong, external relationships with stakeholders and donors that further organizational growth and impact.
* Provide guidance and vision casting to all site staff as well as direct supervision to program leaders. Ensure support to teams in order to create successful impact, smooth and effective site functionality, and strong, healthy teams.

**QUALIFICATIONS** 

All employees will be thoroughly committed to Immerse’s mission. The ideal candidate will embrace Immerse’s values of **with**, **worship**, and **relentless pursuit** (visit our About Page to learn what this means!). All candidates should have the following qualifications and experience:

**Minimum Qualifications**: Master’s Degree in business, psychology, social work, or related field required. 10 or more years of business and/or nonprofit experience, with 7\+ years supervisory/management experience and leading teams.

**Preferred Qualifications:** Passion to see youth from crisis succeed through the collaborative efforts of an array of stakeholders including staff, community members, government, families, and the young people themselves. Prior executive leadership and experience working with a board. Development and communications experience. Experience managing a federally or state supported program. Experience working with diverse funding sources.

**Additional Qualifications:** 

* Possess an entrepreneurial spirit and desire to be a key leader in the organization’s regional presence and growth
* Outstanding presentation and communication skills and the experience and proclivity to be an effective spokesperson, relationship builder, and fundraiser
* Excellent coalition building skills with an ability to communicate and work effectively with a variety of internal and external stakeholders
* Prior experience and success in development and fundraising
* Represent the organization well to the public and be enthusiastic about serving youth from crisis
* Strong commitment to the professional development of staff; successful track record of recruiting and retaining a diverse and high\-performing team

Immerse Arkansas was founded in 2010 with the mission of transforming youth from crisis into overcomers. The nonprofit organization serves youth between the ages of 14 and 24, whose past trauma and challenges have created barriers to becoming independent, healthy, successful adults.

Immerse Arkansas works with these youth and families to address the underlying trauma resulting from abuse or neglect. We believe that when we surround youth from crisis with unconditional relationships, a vision for their restored future, and tools that anticipate their needs and dreams, we create a climate for healing, growth, and transformation.

Immerse is a collaboration of redemptive innovators who pair ambitious faith with strategy in all pursuits, especially anything labeled as “impossible.” We’re hungry for healing for all, and we’re especially interested in those who have been counted out. We are looking for someone who fits

The CDO will inherit strong donor relationships, a signature event with real momentum, an engaged Board, and an affiliated Foundation, and will be asked to create the strategy, systems, campaigns, story, and team that turn those assets into predictable, diversified, and growing revenue; while modeling BGCGW’s mission, vision and priorities.  

We think about revenue in three buckets: individuals and events; foundation, corporate, and government grants; and Program \& Partnership Revenue, meaning contracts, fee\-for\-service programs, and other earned income. Over the next 18 to 24 months, we intend to shift the mix so that recurring and contracted sources carry the majority of our budget, individual giving becomes routine and systematized, grant submissions run on a disciplined pipeline, and our dependence on any single event declines. The CDO owns that transformation.  

The right leader is a fundraiser first: someone who has personally closed six\- and seven\-figure gifts and built the machinery behind them. The right leader is also a storyteller and a modern marketer who understands that visibility drives revenue, and who can make BGCGW impossible to ignore in the DMV. And the right leader understands that a youth\-serving organization must sell what it does well, price it fairly, and partner with counties, school systems, employers, and families to fund it. If you have done all three or done two exceptionally and are hungry to do the third, we want to talk with you.  

Reporting to the President \& CEO and serving on the Executive Leadership Team, the Chief Development Officer is accountable for BGCGW's revenue strategy, forecasting, and results across individual giving, major and principal gifts, institutional grants, corporate partnerships, signature events, and Program \& Partnership Revenue, as well as for the organization's brand, marketing, and communications. The CDO leads, builds, and develops the Resource Development team; partners closely with the Board of Directors, regional Club boards, and the BGCGW Foundation; and serves as a trusted thought partner to the CEO on the organization's financial future and public voice.  

The CDO will personally manage a portfolio of the organization's most important donor and partner relationships while building a team and a system that does not depend on any one person, including the CDO. This position has broad latitude and discretion to formulate business plans and strategies for BGCGW.
Responsibilities:
**Revenue Strategy and Portfolio Leadership**  

* Develop and execute a comprehensive, multi\-year revenue plan aligned with BGCGW's strategic priorities, with clear annual and quarterly targets by revenue stream.
* Own the full revenue portfolio: individual and major gifts, planned giving, foundation and corporate grants, government funding, corporate partnerships and sponsorships, signature events, and Program \& Partnership Revenue.
* Lead the deliberate shift in BGCGW's revenue mix toward recurring, contracted, and diversified sources, and report progress transparently to the CEO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board.
* Partner with the CEO and Finance on revenue forecasting, cash flow planning, and budget development, ensuring every revenue line is grounded in a named prospect, a pipeline stage, and a probability.
* Build a culture of philanthropy across the organization in which every leader understands their role in generating and stewarding resources.

**Major, Principal, and Individual Giving**  

* Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio of the organization's top donors and prospects, including high\-net\-worth individuals, family foundations, and philanthropists at the six\- and seven\-figure level.
* Run a disciplined moves\-management process with clear touchpoint cadences, ask calendars, and stewardship plans, tracked in Salesforce.
* Build a systematic annual giving and mid\-level donor program that converts first\-time and event donors into loyal, multi\-year supporters, with retention and upgrade rates as core metrics.
* Establish a planned giving program and integrate legacy giving into major donor conversations.
* Ensure every gift, at every level, is acknowledged promptly, personally, and accurately.

**Institutional Giving and Grants**  

* Build a mechanized, calendar\-driven grants pipeline covering foundation, corporate, and government (federal, state, county, and city) opportunities, from prospecting through submission, reporting, and closeout.
* Establish clear ownership at every step of the grants process across Resource Development, Operations, Programs, and Finance, so that no deadline, report, or reimbursement is ever missed.
* Grow public funding relationships in DC, Maryland, and Virginia, including county and municipal partnerships that fund Club operations directly.
* Supervise and develop grants staff, and scale the function as the pipeline grows.

**Corporate Partnerships and Signature Events**  

* Lead the strategy for BlueFest, Youth \& Real Estate, and other signature events, keeping them fresh, profitable, and connected to long\-term donor relationships, including recruiting and managing event co\-chairs, committees, and lead sponsors, while intentionally reducing reliance on event revenue over time.
* Build a robust corporate partnership program that diversifies beyond our traditional sectors into new industries across the region, with offerings that extend beyond sponsorship to workforce, volunteer, and cause\-marketing partnerships.
* Apply rigorous return\-on\-investment analysis to every event and partnership.

**Program \& Partnership Revenue**  

* In partnership with Programs and Operations leadership, identify, structure, price, and close fee\-for\-se

Primary Job Functions



The Program Director is responsible for the overall leadership, operation, and development of HERO House Seattle in alignment with the mission of HERO House NW and the Standards for Clubhouse Model of Psychiatric Rehabilitation established by Clubhouse International.



The duties listed below describe the primary responsibilities of the position but are **not intended to be a comprehensive or exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or activities required of the position**. Responsibilities may change or additional duties may be assigned based on organizational and program needs.



Leadership and Clubhouse Operations


* Uphold and advance the mission, goals, objectives, values, and policies of HERO House Seattle and HERO House NW.
* Provide leadership and direction for the daily operation of the Clubhouse consistent with Clubhouse International Standards.
* Develop, implement, and maintain operational procedures that support effective Clubhouse programming.
* Maintain current knowledge of and ensure compliance with HERO House NW organizational policies and procedures.
* Promote a Clubhouse culture centered on meaningful relationships, member participation, recovery, choice, hope, opportunity, and community.
* Ensure Clubhouse operations actively reflect the Standards for Clubhouse Model of Psychiatric Rehabilitation.
* Work collaboratively with the CEO, CPO, staff, members, community partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen and develop the Clubhouse.
* Identify opportunities for program improvement, growth, member engagement, and community partnerships.
* Participate in meetings, trainings, conferences, and professional development activities as appropriate.
* Represent HERO House Seattle with community partners and local, state, national, and Clubhouse\-related organizations.


Staff Leadership and Development


* Hire, onboard, train, supervise, evaluate, develop, and, when necessary, discipline or terminate Program Generalists in accordance with HERO House NW policies.
* Provide staff with clear expectations, regular feedback, coaching, and opportunities for professional development.
* Ensure Program Generalists effectively support members in the Work\-Ordered Day, employment, education, outreach, housing, community support, advocacy, social/recreational opportunities, and other Clubhouse services.
* Foster a collaborative staff culture that encourages initiative, accountability, adaptability, teamwork, and meaningful member participation.
* Ensure staff understand and consistently implement Clubhouse International Standards and HERO House NW policies and procedures.


Program and Member Engagement


* Work side by side with members and staff throughout the Clubhouse Work\-Ordered Day, including participation in assigned units such as Hospitality/Kitchen and Business/Clerical.
* Maintain the Clubhouse's primary responsibility of helping members experience being needed, valued, and meaningfully involved in the work and community of the Clubhouse.
* Actively build productive partnerships with members and encourage participation, leadership, and ownership of Clubhouse activities.
* Facilitate tasks and projects in ways that maximize members' skills, talents, interests, engagement, and leadership.
* Provide positive, supportive relationships that promote hope, choice, wellness, recovery, self\-determination, and personal growth.
* Support programming related to employment, education, housing, outreach, advocacy, social and recreational opportunities, and other member\-identified goals.
* Train, job coach, and support members at employment sites, including Transitional and Supported Employment placements.
* Provide education and resources that support illness self\-management, self\-advocacy, self\-determination, wellness, and shared healthcare decision\-making.
* Help members identify and connect with community\-based services and supports, including primary care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, housing, financial benefits, transportation, and other resources.
* Provide and model effective advocacy to help members access needed services and supports.
* Assist members in identifying, maintaining, or reconnecting with family, friends, and other natural supports when desired by the member.
* Provide or coordinate transportation to employment, appointments, Clubhouse activities, social events, conferences, and other activities when appropriate.


Compliance, Contracts, and Administration


* Provide regular reports and updates to the CEO and CPO to support organizational decision\-making and program oversight.
* Collaborate with the CEO and CPO to ensure compliance with funding contracts, regulatory requirements, licenses, certifications, reporting requirements, and program standards.

* Maintain appropriate records related to Clubhouse operations, program outcomes, member services, staffing, and contractual obligations.
* Ensure concerns involving member safety, emergencies, crises, service gaps, or significant barriers are communicated promptly to appropriate organizational leadership.


Financial and Resource Management


* Operate the Clubhouse within its approved budget.
* Monitor program expenditures and the operating budget on a regular basis.
* Promptly communicate significant budget variances, financial concerns, or resource needs to the CEO and/or CPO.
* Use organizational resources responsibly and support effective stewardship of program funds, equipment, facilities, and other assets.


Scheduling and Travel


* Maintain flexibility to work occasional evenings and weekends based on program needs, employment responsibilities, social activities, special events, or other Clubhouse functions.
* Travel locally and, when necessary, regionally or nationally with members

**Job Overview**

Professional Radiology, Inc. (PRI), a leading independent, physician\-owned radiology practice serving Greater Cincinnati and Northern Kentucky, is seeking an accomplished healthcare executive to serve as its next Chief Executive Officer.

PRI has served the region for more than 50 years and today includes more than 35 radiologists across multiple subspecialties and approximately 50 employees. The practice provides comprehensive diagnostic and interventional radiology services and maintains long\-standing relationships with major hospitals, health systems, and outpatient imaging partners.

THE OPPORTUNITY

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will serve as PRI's senior administrative executive and strategic business leader. The CEO will work closely with the President, physician leadership, and PRI's physician\-led committees to execute the strategic direction established by the Board and position the organization for continued long\-term success.

This is an opportunity to lead a well\-established independent medical practice at a time of significant change in radiology and healthcare. The successful candidate will combine strong executive and business leadership with an appreciation for the culture and governance of a physician\-owned organization.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The CEO will provide leadership across the organization, with particular responsibility for:

* Strategic planning and execution
* Financial performance and long\-range planning
* Hospital and health\-system relationships and contract negotiations
* Physician recruitment, retention, and workforce planning
* Operational performance, quality, and service
* Technology, artificial intelligence, and workflow innovation
* Administrative leadership and organizational development working with the COO and CFO
* Compliance, legal, and enterprise risk management

Quality, and Recruitment \& Retention

**Responsibilities**

* Provide overall strategic direction and leadership for the Professional Radiology division, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
* Lead and manage executive teams, fostering a collaborative and high\-performance work environment.
* Oversee financial management, including budgeting, financial planning, and resource allocation to ensure fiscal responsibility and sustainability.
* Develop and implement strategic initiatives to enhance service quality, operational efficiency, and growth opportunities within radiology services.
* Maintain strong relationships with the Board of Directors, providing regular updates on organizational performance and strategic plans.
* Ensure compliance with industry regulations, standards, and best practices in radiology and healthcare delivery.
* Represent the organization at industry events, professional associations, and community engagements to promote the division's reputation and growth.

**THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE PRI seeks a healthcare executive with significant leadership experience in a physician practice, hospital\-based specialty organization, medical group, health system, or comparable healthcare organization. The successful candidate should demonstrate:**

**Approximately 5 \- 10 years of progressive healthcare leadership experience .** 

Strong financial, operational, and strategic leadership required.

PROFESSIONAL RADIOLOGY, INC.

**Experience working effectively with physicians and physician leadership**

**Experience negotiating complex healthcare or professional services agreements**

**Strong relationship\-building and executive communication skills**

**Experience with physician recruitment, workforce planning, and practice economics**

**Ability to lead organizational change while building consensus and maintaining accountability**

**High standards of integrity, judgment, professionalism, and discretion**

A bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, business, finance, or a related field is required or equivalent related experience. An MBA, MHA, or comparable advanced degree is preferred. Experience with a physician\-owned medical practice or hospital\-based specialty group is strongly preferred. Radiology experience is desirable but not required. LEADERSHIP PROFILE PRI is looking for a CEO who is strategic, financially sophisticated, operationally strong, collaborative, decisive, and relationship\-oriented. The successful candidate must be comfortable working within a physician\-led governance structure and capable of earning the confidence of physician shareholders, employees, hospital executives, and strategic partners. Above all, PRI seeks a leader who understands the value of physician ownership and can help preserve what has made the practice successful while preparing the organization for the future. THE MISSION Strengthen PRI's financial and operational performance, recruit and retain exceptional physicians, deepen hospital partnerships, embrace appropriate innovation, and position Professional Radiology to remain a strong and independent physician\-owned radiology practice for the next generation. Professional Radiology, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Chief Executive

Background


Founded in 2019, Kairos Academies is a public charter school serving around 400 middle and high school students in St. Louis, Missouri. Kairos was founded on the belief that students thrive when they are known deeply, challenged academically, and given increasing ownership of their learning and futures.


This belief is lived through a model that combines rigorous academics with strong relationships and student agency. Every student has a dedicated mentor who serves as a consistent advocate and bridge between school and home. Through Next Prep, a core Kairos program focused on self\-discovery, career exploration, and professional skill\-building, students develop a clear plan for life after graduation and build the skills to pursue their education, income, and life goals. Students also connect their learning to the real world through job site visits, networking, professional skills practice, paid internships, and other college and career experiences.


In 2026, Kairos celebrated one of its most significant milestones to date: graduating its first senior class. This achievement marks an important moment in Kairos’s continued growth and reflects its commitment to preparing students to thrive in the lives they choose after graduation.


As Kairos moves beyond its founding years, the organization enters its next chapter with meaningful momentum and a clearer understanding of where it must continue to grow. Strong school\-based leadership and a renewed focus on instructional excellence are creating greater classroom consistency, supported by strengthened coaching and feedback systems that continue to reinforce a culture of continuous improvement. Kairos also enters this transition with financial stability, providing a strong foundation for the work ahead.


At the same time, Kairos is at an important inflection point. While students have demonstrated meaningful academic growth, increasing proficiency remains a critical priority. Enrollment has also fallen short of the organization’s goals, creating an opportunity to strengthen the student and family experience, rebuild enrollment, and align the organization’s structure and resources with the students it serves. As Kairos looks ahead, its focus is clear: strengthen the core academic program, deepen its connection with students and families, and build the organizational foundation needed for sustainable long\-term impact.


To learn more about Kairos Academies, please visit their website.


Opportunity


Kairos Academies seeks a Chief Executive Officer (CEO) to lead the organization through an important next phase of its development. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the CEO will build on the momentum already underway while bringing the focus, judgment, and disciplined execution needed to translate that progress into stronger, more sustainable outcomes for students.


The next CEO will inherit meaningful organizational capacity, including a deeply committed team, strong school\-based leadership, an increasingly consistent culture of instructional coaching and feedback, and a stable financial foundation. The opportunity now is to build from those strengths: accelerating academic achievement, strengthening enrollment and student persistence, stabilizing the organization’s systems and ways of working, and aligning its structure and resources to create the conditions for sustainable impact over time.


This is an opportunity for a leader who can identify the organization’s most important priorities and thoughtfully sequence the work, make sound decisions about people and resources, and keep Kairos focused on delivering an exceptional experience for students. This role calls for a grounded, hands\-on leader who believes deeply in Kairos’s mission and combines high expectations with humility. The next CEO will lead by building trust across the organization and digging into the work alongside the team while maintaining a clear view of where Kairos is headed.


Key Priorities for the Chief Executive Officer:


* Accelerate academic progress: Build on the instructional momentum underway, set a clear bar for academic excellence, and ensure strong student growth translates into increased proficiency over time
* Strengthen enrollment and student persistence: Develop a comprehensive strategy for attracting and retaining families, improve communication and the consistency of the student and family experience, address practical barriers to enrollment and persistence, and strengthen Kairos’s presence and reputation in St. Louis.
* Stabilize and align the organization for sustainable impact: Clarify priorities, roles, decision rights, and accountability; align Kairos’s people, resources, systems, and organizational structure with its current needs; and build a strong foundation for the future.
* Build and sustain a strong leadership team and culture: Develop and retain strong leaders, establish clear expectations and accountability, and continue building a culture in which people can do their best work.

* Lead Kairos as a credible external partner: Build strong relationships with the Board, families, authorizer, funders, and the broader St. Louis community while representing Kairos with judgment, transparency, and credibility.

jobs.description:
The Dubois County Community Foundation is seeking an accomplished, strategic, and community\-minded leader to serve as its next Executive Director. With approximately $100 million in charitable assets, the Foundation plays an important role in strengthening Dubois County and its communities through philanthropy, partnerships, grantmaking, and thoughtful stewardship of charitable resources.


The Executive Director will serve as the Foundation's chief executive, community ambassador, relationship builder, and strategic leader. Working with an engaged Board of Directors and a dedicated staff, the new leader will guide strategy, strengthen community and donor relationships, grow charitable assets, develop organizational capacity, and ensure strong financial and operational stewardship.


Key Priorities

* Translate the Foundation's mission and strategic plan into impactful results.
* Build and maintain trusted relationships with staff, donors, fundholders, nonprofits, professional advisors, business and civic leaders, and community partners.
* Grow charitable assets through donor development, stewardship, planned giving, and new philanthropic opportunities.
* Partner effectively with the Board on strategy, governance, policy, and long\-range planning.
* Understand emerging community needs and identify opportunities for the Foundation to provide leadership and impact.
* Ensure sound financial, investment, operational, legal, and organizational stewardship.

 **Requirements**  

The successful candidate is a proven leader with strong strategic thinking, organizational leadership, and relationship\-building skills who embraces and models the Foundation’s core values. They demonstrate integrity, accountability, transparency, humility, and professionalism.


Key leadership competencies include:


* Executive\-level leadership and organizational management experience
* Community relationship building and stewardship
* Strategic thinking and the ability to turn vision into action
* Experience leading, developing, engaging and motivating staff
* Donor development, client relationship, or comparable relationship\-management experience
* Nonprofit, foundation, philanthropic, financial, investment, or related business acumen
* Experience working effectively with a governing board
* Excellent communication and public\-speaking skills
* Commitment to fostering a culture of trust, collaboration, positive impact, and innovation

Foundation/nonprofit experience is valuable, but is not required. Exceptional candidates may come from other relevant leadership backgrounds.


Candidates should possess a bachelor's degree and at least ten years of relevant professional experience, or an advanced degree and at least five years of relevant professional experience.


This is a full\-time, salaried position reporting to the Board of Directors and based on\-site in Jasper, Indiana. Relocation to the area is required. The Foundation offers a competitive executive compensation and benefits package appropriate for the scope and responsibilities of the position.

  



  

  

**Benefits**  

The Foundation offers a competitive executive compensation and benefits package including health insurance and paid time off.

**Job Title:** Program Director of Blind and Visually Impaired Support Services


**Position Summary:**

The Program Director of Blind and Visually Impaired Support Services provides leadership and oversight for specialized education services supporting students who are visually impaired, blind, or deaf\-blind across diverse educational settings. The Director ensures effective program operations, staff supervision, compliance with federal and state regulations, and alignment with instructional best practices. The role also manages interagency collaboration, professional development, and budgetary planning to support student access and achievement. This position exists to ensure high\-quality, compliant, and equitable services for students with vision access needs.  



**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Direct program\-level staff, communicating expectations, supporting employee development, and ensuring compliance with AIU policies and practices, thereby aligning the program with the agency.
* Supervise and evaluate personnel ensuring effective service delivery, compliant with students’ IEPs and special education regulations, maintaining quality programming that emphasizes student growth and achievement.
* Recruit, orient, and manage personnel congruent with Human Resources procedures, ensuring positions are filled by personnel with appropriate credentials, so that highly qualified staff are available to deliver specialized services.
* Coordinates and delivers professional development on topics such as instructional practices, technologies, and regulatory requirements ensuring staff and stakeholders remain current and capable when meeting student needs.
* Assign caseloads and manages service delivery systems, informed by regulatory requirements and contractual provisions, such that staff are providing equitable, efficient, and responsive student support.
* Collaborate with schools and districts, agencies, and partners to align services, inform policy, and advocate for students with sensory impairments, safeguarding quality services and influencing system\-level changes to improve learners’ outcomes.
* Represent the program through collaborations with training and consultation partners, institutes of higher education, advocacy groups, and professional organizations to advance matters relating to students with sensory impairments.
* Manage the program budget, maintaining oversight in areas including staffing, resource allocation, and fee\-for\-service rates, in order to support responsible fiscal management and program sustainability.
* Oversee student referrals and evaluations, monitor timelines and documentation, and participates in student team meetings to ensure timely access to appropriate services that comply with regulatory requirements.
* Oversee the maintenance of data systems that include reporting of student service delivery, caseloads, and billing, as well as communicating with internal and external stakeholders about such data, ensuring transparency, accuracy, and informed decision\-making.
* Contributes to policy development and procedural matters that affect the program, including input into collective bargaining, by providing information that safeguards the operations of the program.

Other duties as assigned by the Assistance Executive Director of Special Education and Pupil Services.  

* 
**Qualifications:**

* PA Certification in Special Education or Visually Impaired K\-12 required.
* Pennsylvania Supervisory Certification in Special Education and/or Principal Certification required.

* Five (5\) years of administrative and supervisory experience preferred.

* Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work under pressure.
* Ability to effectively present information and articulately respond to stakeholder inquiries.

* Be able to lift or carry up to 25 pounds.

Additional duties are performed by the individuals currently holding this position and additional duties may be assigned.

----------

jobs.description:
**Hadrian \- Manufacturing the Future**
=======================================


Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full\-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission\-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

  

Following our $1\.37B Series D at a $7\.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory\-as\-a\-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

  

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

  

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**The Role**
------------


This is a dual\-front role built for someone with 15\-20\+ years inside the defense budget process. The core of the job is shaping the budget build inside the Pentagon and OMB, and engaging the process by which Congress sets the defense topline — a process driven heavily by congressional leadership, Armed Services Committee leaders, and the Budget Committees. This role also requires close fluency in how funding is actually spent once it's appropriated — apportionment, allocation, obligation, and execution. Particular depth on how the organic industrial base is managed and funded, how the National Defense Stockpile is managed, defense working capital funds, and the reprogramming process is also desired.


Appropriations Committee engagement and NDAA authorization requests are owned day to day by the Head of Government Relations \- Federal Legislative; this role supports that work rather than leading it. Because this role's core relationships — Pentagon and OMB budget staff, Armed Services Committee and Budget Committee leadership, and the comptroller community — cross executive and legislative branches, it reports directly to the SVP, Public Policy. On Appropriations Committee engagement and NDAA authorization requests, this role works in a dotted\-line partnership with the Head of Government Relations \- Federal Legislative, supporting rather than owning those relationships. Similarly, this role will closely collaborate with the Head of Government Relations – Executive Branch, especially at the White House offices.


This is an individual contributor role to start, built for someone who can operate through expertise, judgment, and relationships rather than headcount. As the budget and execution portfolio matures, the scope is expected to grow — potentially into a small team — but this is not a role that starts with people management built in.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

**Budget Build \& Topline Strategy**

* Own Hadrian's engagement on how the President's Budget request is built inside the Pentagon and OMB, before it ever reaches Congress.
* Build and hold relationships with congressional leadership and the leadership of the House and Senate Armed Services and Budget Committees — the offices most responsible for setting the defense topline — distinct from the appropriations process itself.
* Bring a fluent understanding of the distinction between mandatory and discretionary spending and how the reconciliation process can affect the defense topline, translating that distinction into clear implications for Hadrian.
* Support the Head of Government Relations \- Federal Legislative on Appropriations Committee engagement, on NDAA authorization requests, congressional oversight and and testimony prep, as a dotted\-line partner; represent Hadrian on budget\-build and topline matters directly.
* Translate the federal budget calendar — President's Budget rollout, markups, topline agreements, continuing resolutions — into concrete, timely guidance for the CEO, SVP, the Federal sales lead, and Hadrian's executive team.

**Execution\-Year Budget Management**

* Bring deep fluency in how funding actually moves once appropriated — apportionment, allocation, obligation, and execution — and use that fluency to anticipate rather than just react to funding shifts affecting Hadrian.
* Understand closely how the organic industrial base is managed and funded, and flag where Hadrian's factories and public private partnership plans intersect with those investment decisions.
* Understand closely how the National Defense Stockpile is managed and funded, and where it bears on Hadrian's business.
* Own oversight of defense working capital funds and the reprogramming process — including above\- and below\-threshold reprogramming and the omnibus reprogramming action — especially how to influence reprogrammings prior to submission to the congressional defense committees.
* Operate proactively, not reactively: identify and help Hadrian seize opportunities during the year of execution, and surface and mitigate risk before it becomes a problem.

**Budget Intelligence \& Internal Advisory**

* Partner with the Federal sales and capture teams to make sure budget\-build, topline, and execution\-year intelligence directly informs pursuit strategy, pricing, and timing on Hadrian's federal opportunities.
* Prepare board\- and investor\-facing materials on federal budget risk and opportunity exposure as needed.

**What We’re Looking For**

**Aunt Lute Books Co\-Executive Director in Administration Job Posting**

**About the Organization**

Aunt Lute Books is a 44\-year\-old non profit, intersectional feminist press dedicated to publishing literature by writers who have traditionally been underrepresented or excluded from the literary canon. For more than four decades, Aunt Lute has championed bold, boundary\-pushing fiction, to create space for voices and perspectives too often marginalized within mainstream publishing.

**About the Position**

Aunt Lute is seeking a motivated and collaborative **Co\-Executive Director in Administration** to help co\-lead the organization through its next stage of growth and sustainability. This part\-time position (20\-22 hours per week) works in partnership with the Co\-Executive Director in Operations. The Co\-Executive Director in Administration will focus primarily on fundraising, grant writing and resource development, financial oversight, organizational growth and strategic planning, community engagement and Board relations. They will uphold Aunt Lute’s mission and values in their leadership and decision\-making. This is a hybrid position based in San Francisco. Ideally, candidates should be able to work in\-person once a week and attend events.

*\*See Addendum below for Co\-Executive Director in Operations responsibilities.*

**Job Responsibilities:**

Development

* In collaboration with the Board of Directors, creating and implementing fundraising plans that primarily focus on private foundations and individual annual donors.
* Working closely with staff and Board to accomplish revenue goals consisting of major gifts, foundation and government grants.

Financial Management

* Having a daily knowledge of where financial matters stand for the organization, which includes providing transparent fiscal stewardship that maintains a positive financial position and adequate control and accounting of all funds.
* Develop and propose an annual budget to the Board for their approval.
* Working with our accounting consultant to reconcile accounts and to write tax reports including city, state, and federal reports as required.

Organizational Growth

* With the Board of Directors, creating short\- and long\-term strategic plans in support of Aunt Lute’s mission and documenting progress towards achieving them.
* Developing and improving organizational infrastructure, including business processes, systems, policies, and tools, to maximize efficiency and future growth.

Community Engagement/Outreach

* Participating in relevant community events and cultivating speaking skills to deepen local networks, engage new donors, and expand community presence.
* Developing and nurturing positive relationships with other arts and cultural organizations.
* Supporting staff in planning and executing events sponsored by Aunt Lute in partnership with mission\-aligned organizations.
* Practice feminist leadership styles and ability to engage with racial/gender equity organizations.

Staff Management

* Work with the Co\-ED in Operations to manage the recruitment, employment, and release of all personnel while implementing sound human resource practices.
* Co\-managing the oversight of employee performance and delegating responsibilities.
* Promoting a work culture that is inclusive, equitable, transparent, and respectful of all backgrounds and identities.

Board Relations

* Support the board in recruiting and identifying prospective members who bring diverse skills, perspectives, and strong commitment to Aunt Lute’s mission.
* Maintaining regular communication with the Board Chair through regular check\-ins, and attending and supporting preparation for Board meetings, held every other month to advance organizational priorities and implement strategic planning.
* Providing leadership in developing program, organizational, and financial plans with the Board.

**Required Skills for this Position:**

Required skills and qualifications:

* 3 or more years in non\-profit organizational management within publishing, literary arts, or cultural organizations
* 3 years of experience in managing budgets; considerable experience working with spreadsheets (Microsoft Excel)
* Experience in grant writing, fundraising, and donor relations
* Demonstrated commitment to equitable and transparent collaboration with colleagues
* Highly competent in verbal, written, and visual communication
* Proximity to or ability to commute to the Bay Area for in\-person meetings and events

Preferred skills and qualifications:

* Experience working with a nonprofit Board of Directors
* Experience with fundraising tech platforms
* Knowledgeable with Social Media and Publicity
* Experience with QuickBooks

**Compensation:**

* $34\-$38/hour for 20 hours per week

**How to Apply:** 

Email a resume and cover letter addressed to Aunt Lute Search Committee to jobs@auntlute.com*.* 

Cover letters should address how applicants believe their qualifications, experience, aspirations, and values align with Aunt Lute’s publishing mission. Review of applications will begin on November 1, 2026, and applications will be accepted until the position is filled. If selected for an interview, candidates will be asked to complete an online questionnaire and provide references.

**\*Addendum**

**The Co\-Executive Director in Operations is responsible for:**

* Accounts payable, receivable, banking, and account reconciliation
* Working with the accountant on account reconciliation and end of the year reporting.
* Reporting to the accountant as they close the financial year: on payroll, inventory, sales, etc.
* Payroll and related financial reporting
* Book inventory management, reprints, and shipping
* Serving as liaison with Aunt Lute’s distributor, Ingram
* Overseeing royalty calculations
* Coordinating logistics for book fairs, events, and conferences
* Reporting to the Board on forthcoming book releases, sales, cash and investments, and other operational matter

Mount Sopris Montessori School \| Carbondale, Colorado

In\-person \| Full\-time \| Salaried, exempt

**Salary range: $90,000–$130,000 annually**

About Us

Located on a quiet residential street in the beautiful mountain town of Carbondale, Colorado, Mount Sopris Montessori School is a nonprofit preschool serving about 60 children ages 18 months through 6 years. Founded in 1981 by Kathryn and Mark Ross, the not\-for\-profit school is recognized as an exceptional preschool environment, based on the Montessori Method of child\-led learning. The school offers dedicated preschool and toddler classrooms led by experienced educators, with teachers certified through organizations such as the American Montessori Society (AMS), American Montessori International (AMI), or the North American Montessori Center (NAMC).

Position Summary

We seek a director who recognizes the critical importance of an inspired preschool education. Preschool is a critical educational period because roughly 90% of a child’s brain development happens before age five, laying the foundational cognitive, social, and emotional habits for life.

The Executive Director provides strategic, financial, and organizational leadership for Mount Sopris Montessori School. The Executive Director sets direction in partnership with the Board of Directors, holds ultimate accountability for the school's financial health and regulatory standing, and leads the Assistant Director and staff in delivering a high\-quality Montessori program. Montessori training is provided as part of onboarding.

*This role reports to the Board of Directors (via the Board President) and directly supervises the Assistant Director, who manages day\-to\-day school operations. This is a Colorado Department of Early Childhood (CDEC) “Director of Record” position — the Executive Director carries ultimate licensing accountability for the center.*

Key Responsibilities

**Governance \& Strategy**

* Partner with the Board to set and execute annual and multi\-year strategic plan and priorities.
* Translate Board\-approved strategy into operational goals for the Assistant Director and staff.

* Lead fundraising and development: annual giving, donor relationships, grants, and events.

**Facilities Oversight \& Management**

* Identify and plan for capital improvements and major facility expenditures in partnership with the Board.

**Licensing, Compliance \& Community**

* Maintain staff qualifications, background checks, and training records for CDEC compliance.
* Represent the school within the Carbondale and Roaring Fork Valley community.
* Set enrollment strategy and monitor overall enrollment against budget.
* Champion the school's Montessori philosophy and educational quality standards.

Full\-time, in\-person, Monday–Friday during school operating hours, with occasional evenings or weekends for Board meetings and school events.

About Evergreen Goodwill
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill of Northwest Washington is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit organization founded in 1923 that helps people get jobs across Northwest Washington by offering high\-quality free job training, education and job placement. Goodwill empowers individuals to overcome barriers to working, by providing comprehensive support and connecting them with life changing job opportunities, ensuring they are career\-ready and can support themselves and their families.
  
  

The organization employs over 2,000 people, operates five job\-training centers, 23 nonprofit retail stores and more than 27 donation sites in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom and Kitsap Counties. Every day, Evergreen Goodwill connects people with the jobs, services and skills they need — because Jobs Change Lives. We are committed to creating and sustaining a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion (DEI) and are focused on creating a joyful, inclusive and successful organization.
  
  

**Job Title:** Executive Director, Evergreen Goodwill Education Center
  
**Location:** Evergreen Goodwill Job Training \& Education Center \- Seattle, WA
  
**Salary Range:** $180,000–$220,000
  
  

Evergreen Goodwill is seeking a Founding Executive Director to build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center (EGEC), a new organization formed to operate Washington State’s first adult high school using the Goodwill Education Initiatives model. Over the next decade, the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center plans to launch at least five Excel Centers—public high schools for adults ages 18 and older—in King, Snohomish, Skagit, Whatcom, and Kitsap counties. Washington’s Excel Centers will build on the national Goodwill Excel Center model, which now includes 50 campuses across 11 states and Washington, D.C. The model combines rigorous academics, wraparound services, and life coaching to help adult students earn high school diplomas.
  
The Executive Director will shape the execution strategy, build the organization, launch its schools, beginning with Excel Center Goodwill Dearborn in Seattle, and lead them toward long\-term success.
  
We are looking for an executive and builder who can define a bold strategy, translate it into action, and deliver on the promise of these schools. This leader will build and inspire a team, deliver strong student outcomes, engage funders and community partners, advocate for the schools, build an effective board and collaborate with its members, and create a financially and operationally sustainable institution.
  
About The Excel Center
  
The Excel Center model is a tuition\-free public high school designed to help adults earn a state\-recognized diploma, not a GED, along with college credits or industry certifications. Flexible schedules, life coaching, childcare, and transportation support help students balance school with work and family responsibilities. Excel Center graduates earn more than a diploma: they gain college credits and professional certifications that open doors to higher\-paying careers in high\-growth fields. A University of Notre Dame LEO study of the Excel Center model in Indiana found that, five years after graduation, graduates earn 38% more and are significantly more likely to work in fields with career pathways, such as healthcare.
  
Evergreen Goodwill will bring the model to Washington and build on it. We aspire to open an Excel Center in each of the five counties where we operate, ultimately reaching 1,000–1,500 students within the next decade. The founding Executive Director will benefit from a proven model and significant training, guidance, and ongoing support from Goodwill Education Initiatives (GEI), the national experts behind The Excel Center, while shaping the school to meet the needs of our local community. A combination of public funding, including charter school funding, and private philanthropy will support the school.
  
**Learn more about the national Excel Center model:** https://www.goodwillexcelcenter.org/
  
  

**Five key functions of this role include:**  

1\. Academic Excellence, Curriculum Oversight, and Student Outcomes
  
2\. Culture, Talent, and Organizational Leadership
  
3\. Student Recruitment, Enrollment and Retention
  
4\. Partnerships, Board Engagement, Fundraising, and External Leadership
  
5\. Financial Management, Compliance and Accountability
  
What You’ll Do
  
* Build and lead the Evergreen Goodwill Education Center organization. You’ll hire and supervise the Excel Center principals and help build a team that includes teachers, special education and language teachers, coaches, a registrar, and an office manager. You’ll build the school culture, academic program, operations, systems, and infrastructure and put strong academic leadership and expertise in place to support the educational program.
* Shape the operational and growth strategy for the Excel Centers in Washington, translating a proven national model into exceptional public high schools for adults ages 18 and older that are responsive to their local communities.
* Set ambitious goals for enrollment, persistence, graduation, and postsecondary success, using data and accountability to drive strong student outcomes.
* Ensure the financial and operational health of the organization and its schools by overseeing budgeting, staffing, resource allocation, accreditation, charter requirements, and regulatory compliance.
* Serve as the external leader for the Excel Centers, building strong relationships with the board, funders, employers, colleges, community organizations, public leaders, and other partners while leading fundraising, advocacy, and policy engagement for the schools.
* Build a sustainable institution with the visibility, partnerships, funding, and organizational strength to deepen its impact and support expansion across the five counties Evergreen Goodwill serves.

**Overview**

**Director of Operations and Finance** Job Summary

The Director of Operations and Finance supports the financial and administrative operations of Tennessee Caregiver Coalition. Working closely with the President \& CEO, the Director of Operations and Finance manages grant applications and reporting, coordinates the monthly financial close, processes payroll, and maintains systems that help the organization meet its obligations to staff, funders, and caregivers. This is a hands\-on, part\-time role for someone who can manage deadlines, work accurately with financial information, and identify issues early.

This is a part\-time position based in the Nashville office, with a schedule of 12 hours per week during the hours of Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. During the first three months of employment, all scheduled hours will be worked in the office as part of onboarding. Upon successful completion of this period, the employee will be eligible for a hybrid schedule, with at least one in\-office day per week and additional in\-office time as needed. The specific schedule will be set in consultation with the President \& CEO.

This position has the potential to grow into a full\-time Chief Operating Officer role if additional grant funding is secured and organizational needs support the expansion. Any change in hours, title, or responsibilities would be determined by the Tennessee Caregiver Coalition at that time.

This position includes a six\-month probationary assessment period, with a performance review at 90 days and a final review at the six\-month mark to assess progress, long\-term fit, and success in the role. Continuation in the role is contingent upon meeting established performance standards.

The Tennessee Caregiver Coalition is committed to actively cultivating and preserving a culture of equity, inclusion and connectedness. We strive to create a space that enables everyone to bring their full self to the work and that embraces the full spectrum of humanity. These values permeate all aspects of our work.

We are committed to equitable hiring, training, promotional practices, and policies. We value the unique contributions people bring in terms of education, opinions, culture, ethnicity, race, sex, gender identity and expression, nation of origin, age, languages spoken, veteran’s status, color, marital status, religion, ability, sexual orientation, and beliefs. **We strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply.**

Key Responsibilities and Measurable Performance Standards

**Agency Culture \& Leadership**

* Maintain a positive, solutions\-focused attitude, ensuring:
* 100% of interactions with staff, volunteers, and partners are respectful, professional, and encouraging
* Concerns and challenges are addressed constructively, with a focus on problem\-solving rather than negativity
* Personal stress and frustrations are managed in a way that does not negatively impact the workplace environment
* Demonstrate commitment to TCC values in action, ensuring:
* Decisions, interactions, and leadership actions align with TCC’s mission and values
* Proactively models agency values in everyday work, including integrity, accountability, and compassion
* Commitment to equity and inclusion, ensuring:
* Actively participates in agency\-wide equity and inclusion efforts
* Addresses bias and inequities within programs and operations in a thoughtful and proactive manner
* Ensures staff, volunteers, and program participants feel valued, respected, and included
* Support a collaborative and morale\-boosting work environment, ensuring:
* Encourages teamwork, open communication, and mutual respect among staff
* Addresses agency morale concerns within two weeks when issues arise
* Recognizes and celebrates staff successes and program achievements regularly
* Attends and contributes positively to all staff meetings and agency discussions

**Grants \& Contracts**

* Maintain a calendar of grant application, reporting, and contract deadlines.
* Research and identify new grant opportunities that align with Tennessee Caregiver Coalition’s mission, programs, and funding priorities.
* Assess eligibility, funding requirements, and organizational capacity; recommend promising opportunities to the CEO.
* Lead the development and submission of new grant applications, working with the CEO and program staff to prepare proposals, budgets, and supporting materials.
* Coordinate and prepare grant applications, budgets, renewals, and required attachments in partnership with the CEO and program staff.
* Prepare grant reports by gathering financial and program information, checking it for completeness, and submitting reports on time.
* Track grant spending and deliverables, and alert the CEO to potential shortfalls, restrictions, or compliance concerns.
* Maintain organized grant and contract records.

**Financial Operations**

* Coordinate the monthly financial close with the bookkeeper or accountant, including reviewing transactions, reconciliations, grant coding, and outstanding items.
* Prepare monthly financial reports and explain significant budget variances to the CEO.
* Monitor accounts receivable, including state reimbursement requests and outstanding payments, and provide regular cash flow updates.
* Review the status of accounts payable and upcoming obligations so the CEO can plan for payroll, voucher reimbursements, and other expenses.
* Help prepare the annual organizational budget and grant budgets.
* Coordinate the information needed for the annual audit or financial review and required financial filings.

**Payroll and Operational Systems** 

* Run payroll accurately and on schedule, including reviewing time records, approved changes, and payroll reports.
* Maintain written procedures and a reliable calendar for recurring financial, payroll, and grant tasks.
* Identify ways to improve accuracy, documentation, and coordination across financial and program systems

**Job Description**


Embracing Virginia Tech’s core values of Integrity, Service, Honor, Excellence, and Strong Together, and guided by our motto, Ut Prosim (That I May Serve), the Director of Development Strategy and Analytics drives data\-driven innovation and strategic alignment for Athletics fundraising and development, while supporting broader revenue and engagement priorities across the Department of Athletics. Reporting to the Associate AD of Development, Major Gifts, this role manages day\-to\-day analytics operations and acts as a vital bridge between complex data systems, athletic department administrators, and advancement leaders.
  

  

The Director oversees the development of analytical tools, data resources, and visualization reporting platforms to maximize revenue generation, expand fan engagement, and inform Athletics fundraising and revenue strategy. In addition, this position provides a crucial strategic partnership to fundraising and development teams. By applying a sophisticated, data\-driven lens to the philanthropic pipeline, the Director delivers actionable intelligence on fundraiser metrics, portfolio health, and donor trends and translates data into recommendations that inform fundraising strategy and decision\-making. Collaborating across internal departments—development, prospect research, and ticketing—the Director builds best\-in\-class analytics capabilities that streamline performance tracking, uncover growth opportunities, and fuel the long\-term competitive and financial excellence of Virginia Tech Athletics. The Director regularly synthesizes complex fundraising, donors, ticketing, and engagement data into clear insights and recommendations for Hokie Club and Athletics leadership.


**Required Qualifications**


Master's degree in business Analytics, Data Science, Information Systems, Sports Management, Economics, or a related field; or bachelor's degree with experience equating to an advanced degree.
  

  

Proven experience in analytics, business intelligence, or strategic operations.
  

  

Experience working with large datasets and advanced analytics tools.
  

  

Functional familiarity with sports technology platforms, specifically CRM and ticketing systems.
  

  

High proficiency in Microsoft Excel for data analysis, reporting, and visualization.
  

  

Proven skill using database software to analyze reports and present findings via Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.
  

  

Demonstrated ability to analyze complex data, identify meaningful trends, and translate findings into actionable recommendations for leadership and non\-technical audiences.
  

  

Demonstrated experience developing dashboards, performance metrics, KPIs, or other analytical tools to support organizational decision\-making.
  

  

Demonstrated ability to manage tasks and competing deadlines with high speed, accuracy, and sharp attention to detail.
  

  

Self\-motivated and adaptable to working both independently and in close team environments.
  

  

Exceptional communication, strong professionalism, and the ability to interact effectively with diverse individuals in an inclusive environment.
  

  

Proven sound judgment and absolute discretion when handling confidential information.


**Preferred Qualifications**


Direct experience in an NCAA Division I "Power 4" collegiate athletics department or a professional sports analytics environment.
  

  

Professional experience in higher education, collegiate athletics, nonprofits, or marketing.
  

  

Proficiency with data visualization tools.
  

  

Familiarity with advanced features in Microsoft Excel.
  

  

Proven experience defining goals and establishing Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) to measure success.

Exempt: Not eligible for overtime

Regular

$85,000\-$95,000

40\+

October 19th, 2026

Safe Driving Record


The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal conviction check.


**About Virginia Tech**


Dedicated to its motto, *Ut Prosim* (That I May Serve), Virginia Tech pushes the boundaries of knowledge by taking a hands\-on, transdisciplinary approach to preparing scholars to be leaders and problem\-solvers. A comprehensive land\-grant institution that enhances the quality of life in Virginia and throughout the world, Virginia Tech is an inclusive community dedicated to knowledge, discovery, and creativity.  Verland is seeking a **Regional Program Director of Residential Services CLA** who is responsible for the overall leadership, coordination, and operational oversight of a designated group of CLA residential homes within a specific region. **Job Title:** Program Director of Blind and Visually Impaired Support Services


**Position Summary:**

The Program Director of Blind and Visually Impaired Support Services provides leadership and oversight for specialized education services supporting students who are visually impaired, blind, or deaf\-blind across diverse educational settings. The Director ensures effective program operations, staff supervision, compliance with federal and state regulations, and alignment with instructional best practices. The role also manages interagency collaboration, professional development, and budgetary planning to support student access and achievement. This position exists to ensure high\-quality, compliant, and equitable services for students with vision access needs.  



**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Direct program\-level staff, communicating expectations, supporting employee development, and ensuring compliance with AIU policies and practices, thereby aligning the program with the agency.
* Supervise and evaluate personnel ensuring effective service delivery, compliant with students’ IEPs and special education regulations, maintaining quality programming that emphasizes student growth and achievement.
* Recruit, orient, and manage personnel congruent with Human Resources procedures, ensuring positions are filled by personnel with appropriate credentials, so that highly qualified staff are available to deliver specialized services.
* Coordinates and delivers professional development on topics such as instructional practices, technologies, and regulatory requirements ensuring staff and stakeholders remain current and capable when meeting student needs.
* Assign caseloads and manages service delivery systems, informed by regulatory requirements and contractual provisions, such that staff are providing equitable, efficient, and responsive student support.
* Collaborate with schools and districts, agencies, and partners to align services, inform policy, and advocate for students with sensory impairments, safeguarding quality services and influencing system\-level changes to improve learners’ outcomes.
* Represent the program through collaborations with training and consultation partners, institutes of higher education, advocacy groups, and professional organizations to advance matters relating to students with sensory impairments.
* Manage the program budget, maintaining oversight in areas including staffing, resource allocation, and fee\-for\-service rates, in order to support responsible fiscal management and program sustainability.
* Oversee student referrals and evaluations, monitor timelines and documentation, and participates in student team meetings to ensure timely access to appropriate services that comply with regulatory requirements.
* Oversee the maintenance of data systems that include reporting of student service delivery, caseloads, and billing, as well as communicating with internal and external stakeholders about such data, ensuring transparency, accuracy, and informed decision\-making.
* Contributes to policy development and procedural matters that affect the program, including input into collective bargaining, by providing information that safeguards the operations of the program.

Other duties as assigned by the Assistance Executive Director of Special Education and Pupil Services.  

* 
**Qualifications:**

* PA Certification in Special Education or Visually Impaired K\-12 required.
* Pennsylvania Supervisory Certification in Special Education and/or Principal Certification required.
* Five (5\) years of teaching experience in the field of Visually Impaired K\-12 preferred.
* Five (5\) years of administrative and supervisory experience preferred.

* Ability to prioritize tasks, meet deadlines, and work under pressure.
* Ability to effectively present information and articulately respond to stakeholder inquiries.
* Excellent written and oral communication skills.
* Skilled in the use of productivity tools and willingness to work with new technologies.
* PA Driver’s license and reliable transportation required for travel throughout Allegheny County.
* Ability to comply with the AIU Conduct Policy.
**Additional Requirements:**

* Current Act 114, Act 34 and Act 151 and NSOR Certificates required prior to an offer (Must be dated within 1 year of hire date).
* School Personnel Health Record (Form H511\.340 (8/2011\) must be completed and received by Human Resources prior to hire date.

* Be able to lift or carry up to 25 pounds.
* Be able to bend or twist at the neck and back.
